## Summary

This draft PR adds a reviewable, source-bound Round 15 artifact package for
terminal-accumulator elimination on the replayed h=24 complex producer.

The finite candidate has conditional

    κ = 2188324161643 / 20000000000000000
      = 1.0941620808215e-4.

At the time of submission this is approximately 0.124% above the updated
public PR114 value 1.09281094468e-4. The result remains conditional on the
inherited stopped-product, Gaussian normal-form, streaming, fixed-tape,
analytic, and all-size assembly interfaces.

## Construction

After PR118's replayed graph and PR114's saturated placement, 393 terminal
auxiliary roles are removed. Each has no outgoing auxiliary use and one
ordinary output. Its incoming updates are redirected to that output at their
original gate indices and frames. The complete before/after packet is

    [m-h+σ, 1, F-σ, h-1-M]  ->  [m, F-M, 0, 0].

For 0 <= σ <= M <= F <= h-1, the latter strictly majorizes the former.
This proves improvement for every strictly concave power cost, including all
576 paid child-width hinge functions. Target-front moves, source snapshots,
cleanup, and reflected signed inverse operations are charged explicitly.

## Verification

The package includes:

- exact integer adjoint and all-input Q(i) dirty identity;
- exact source-time redirect chronology;
- forward and signed reflected frame traces;
- complete paid histogram and scalar guard;
- six actual malformed-witness rejection tests;
- portable exact assembly receipt with accepted and next-grid-rejected κ.

The main report is `research/terminal-elision/ROUND15_RESEARCH_REPORT.md`.
The checkpoint, exact word, receipts, source hashes, and reproduction scripts
are in the same directory. No pinned upstream worktree was modified.

This is a draft research artifact for review; it does not claim an
unconditional multiplication theorem or a practical runtime benchmark.

**Conditional kappa = 142205877210807 / 200000000000000000 = 0.000711029386054035.**

This extends the pinned [PR249](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/249) construction at `96495746c786d6d0339dbb38c7f553d4af3f88ed`. It improves the preceding 132-pair result, 0.00071046520063283, by approximately **0.0794%**. This is a checked finite construction under the retained public all-size hypotheses, not a claim of an unconditional multiplication theorem or the current leaderboard record.

## Construction

Instead of restricting cancellation to equal pairs of helper response columns, select several simultaneous zero-response directions. Share donor lifts when their frames form nested chains, replace singular common frames by explicitly checked nondegenerate subframes, and place compatible transformations at four actual cuts in the physical program. Every added basis operation and its inverse is charged.

The resulting construction admits **518 pivot entrances**, removes **1344 raw rank units** and **27,772 initial compensation reads**, and pays **1,542 basis/inverse gates**. The literal bank stock is **867,175**. COPY sources are checked for immutability throughout every actual COPY/ERASE window; membership in a selected pivot family alone is not an invalidation.

## Verification

The portable verifier regenerates the pinned upstream word, compiles seven C++ checkers, emits the modified word from its frozen witness, and checks:

- Every one of 20,107 local formal input columns, forward and inverse, with nonvacuous omitted-basis controls.
- 911,680 per-cut kernel equalities, exact arbitrary-precision frame geometry, and all 24 COPY/ERASE windows.
- 518 projector charts and all 3,317,400 bank assignments, with endpoint and omission/repetition controls.
- All 23,627 global five-stage formal columns, including the charged center copies.
- The complete finite invoice, payload and coefficient guards, exact rational recurrence price, all 47 strict outer inequalities, and pinned-baseline regression.

The verifier also requires the generated word hash and all seven mathematical receipts to match the frozen expected results.

## Reproduce

From `research/multicut-kernel-condensation`, with Python 3.11+, a C++17 GNU compiler and Boost headers installed:

```sh
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python verify.py --output ../multicut-replay
```

Use a new output directory. The default regenerates upstream data from the included pinned sources. `--snapshots-only` explicitly records weaker provenance and is not the default. No network or credentials are required during replay.

## Scope

Retains the public all-size compiler, common weighted chart, restored-row, routing, prime, precision/recovery, complex correctness and analytic interfaces. This package does not independently prove those general interfaces, claim a practical multiplication speedup, or supply Lean certification. Larger cube-redesign experiments are excluded from the claimed exponent.

Original source licenses and attributions are preserved. The package contains source, frozen witnesses, proofs and expected receipts; no executable binaries are included.

## Result and comparison

This adds `research/e8-whole-pool-portfolio`, a reproducible conditional construction with

$$T(n)=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{253308389885063}{200000000000000000}=0.001266541949425315.$$

That is **+0.04820338% over #451** (`0.001265931727546219`). The complex supplier binds.
This is a conditional finite artifact, not an unconditional multiplication theorem or Lean certificate.
It does **not** claim to beat #453's higher posted number: #451 supplies a trace obstruction to the
cross-family splitting derivation used there. This construction keeps every residual in one whole family.

## Two construction mechanisms

1. **Whole-residual pooling across replicas.** Allocate the eight replicas jointly rather than solve
   identical per-replica integer packing problems. Every helper stays on one physical array family,
   with a complete slot isometry, a disjoint orthogonal block, and its checked idle window. Both actual
   family and absolute coordinate identities are audited. Complex delta relative to the selected #451
   idle inventory is `{1:-2,7:+8,16:-8,55:+6,64:-4}`. Rank mass stays unchanged; the moment improves.
2. **Invocation-specific complete-program portfolio.** Five reverse calls at stage 5, replicas 0..4,
   use a fully checked rank147 provider; the other 83 use rank149. Each variant adds two residual
   coordinates and changes its local profile by `{1:-2,4:-4,5:+4}`. Whole-owner pooling pays those ten
   additional coordinates by changing a remaining rank52 child to rank42. The full difference from
   uniform pooled rank149 is `{1:-10,4:-20,5:+20,52:-1,42:+1}`. This improves bit-side reserve; it gives
   no further final-kappa increase while the complex supplier binds.

These use whole-slot reindexing/orthogonal-idempotent composition and equal complete-map substitution,
respectively. Structural sources include Mathlib's block-diagonal multiplication and the project's
MUB projection-factor identities. They are sources of mathematical analogies, not Lean certificates
for this artifact. #450 target mixing and two historical partial-prefix recoveries are also used,
but are explicitly credited as prior techniques rather than presented as additional new mechanisms.

## Exact invoice

| Supplier | Window | Live | Physical | Rank mass | Deficit | Maximum child |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Bit | 78 | 9600 | 9609 | 745536 | 3264 | 56 |
| Complex | 89 | 9600 | 10178 | 851136 | 3264 | 64 |

Bit profile: `{1:217742,2:93314,3:23976,4:30912,5:8732,6:5752,7:5168,8:792,42:1,56:444}`.
Complex profile: `{1:170358,2:68992,3:18624,4:19712,5:38336,7:3840,8:9792,55:6,64:1732}`.
Both actual profiles are priced together. Independent proposed gains are never added.

The coefficient bound charges all 88 chronological calls and all bridges, even with foreign-replica
hosting. Route-extra3 and 100,000 finite dispatch operations are charged. The bit row cover is19,431;
the retained complex fractional-depth row reserve is20,161 with its explicit cutoff condition.
Both exact moment engines, six bootstrap levels, and all47 strict outer inequalities are used.

## Reproduction and validation

```sh
python -B research/e8-whole-pool-portfolio/verify.py /absolute/path/to/new-output-directory
```

Requires Python3.11+, SymPy, a C++17 compiler and Boost headers; set `CXX`/`BOOST_INCLUDE` if needed.
No network, optimizer, SciPy, prebuilt binaries, or Lean installation is required. Assertions must be enabled.

Fresh validation reconstructs both complete local providers, all980 dirty columns each, eleven-stage
orientation checks, exact Gram/prime witnesses, and all74,720 columns of the heterogeneous unbanked
controller. It checks65,120 whole bit helpers and49,280 whole complex helpers, physical-axis collisions,
phase recipes, emitted instruction digests,19 bit routing mutants and10 complex routing mutants.
The exact final profiles/templates match the frozen expected invoice. See `VALIDATION.json` and
`REPLAY-MANIFEST.json` for the source-bound replay; `MANIFEST.json` covers final upload contents.
Unchanged public verification chains were not redundantly rerun: inherited complex Clifford evidence
is explicitly retained with its source bindings.

All-size compiler, arbitrary-correlated dirty hosting, target-label, compressed-window, restored-work,
common-grid/tape, precision, and analytic contracts remain inherited assumptions. Finite controls do
not prove these contracts. No global packing optimality or literature-wide priority claim is made.

## Sources, rejected routes, and future work

Direct sources and inspirations include #451 (rank149 whole-host baseline, row bound and trace review),
#450 (target mixing only), #445/#447 (eleven-stage schedules), #443/#439/#417 (response kernels and
residual isometries), #442 (whole idle-family hosting), #433 (complex split-centre/source-basis work),
#425/#386/#370 (mutable basis, geometry and producer), #401/#404 (shared donors/prefix recovery),
and #315's rational outer-assembly lineage. #453 supplied a useful source collection/local comparison;
its split-based price and #448's disputed splitting step are not used. #452 was reviewed but not used.
Exact head pins and licenses are in `PROVENANCE.md`, source headers, and `notices/`.

`RESEARCH.md` preserves the actual discoveries, bounded searches, library analogies, rejected coordinate
splitting attempt, and future routes. Early placement checks on the split attempt did not establish an
operator identity; those larger prices are expressly withdrawn. Product-coordinate factorization must
not be confused with a direct sum of independent array families. The next useful search variables are
larger whole-owner pools and independently correct complex-program portfolios, always with actual
operator semantics and a complete shared invoice.

Developed with OpenAI assistance. No claim of an independent all-size theorem or exclusive priority.

prs.body:
Method and knowledge package on the R715 bit word (PR #463): **what sets the width of a residual, how many narrow residuals the shared-donor kernel can give on the retimed R715 word with coordinate entrances (the verified residual-isometry format: exactly 112), and a 112-pivot kernel selection by seeded annealing.** Conditional **κ = 1294233365881801/1000000000000000000 ≈ 1.294233365881801·10⁻³, bit-bound**: +0.838% over #463
and +0.165% over #472 (κ = 1.292099559·10⁻³). It is below the current lemma-less frontier: −0.108% vs #473 (κ = 1.295630·10⁻³, as updated on Oct 11, now the frontier) and −0.098% vs #478 (1.295509·10⁻³). This PR's point is the method and the bounds, not the frontier. The bit supplier is c = 1295910576589222380953/10²⁴ ≈ 1.295911·10⁻³ (+0.839% over R715). Same word, same
hosting rule, same mixing, #458's complex supplier unchanged: only the kernel selection changes, 84 → 112 pivots.

| side | supplier | endpoint |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| bit (binds) | R715 word, **112 rank-1 kernel pivots**, eleven stages, #442 whole-residual hosting, target mixing | c ≈ 1.295911·10⁻³ |
| complex | #458 paid-adapter kernel, unchanged | b ≈ 1.297204·10⁻³ |

**What is new**
1. **The width rule, checked exactly.** A residual's width is 8 − entrance rank, and only kernel pivots have a nonzero entrance: the helper hierarchy and the
   target mixing do not set it. Checked three ways on all 715 helpers (kernel-word frames, exported records of the mixed word, the independent hosted audit).
2. **The pivot ceiling and the exact maximum, for coordinate entrances** (the verified residual-isometry format). A pivot needs a frame line inside its first frame (263 of 706 helpers), and its delivery vector must be an XOR of donors of one
   entrance class. *Proved:* pivots ≤ |C| − rank = 263 − 86 = **177**, and rank-1 coordinate entrances lose nothing up to parity. *Exact maximum on the retimed R715 word: **112**, by a computer-assisted exhaustive search (independently re-audited), certified by
   `code/exact_pivots.py`* (rerun by `verify.py --light`, asserted equal to 112, about 10 s): the pivot problem is a min-sum-rank list partition (max pivots = |C| − min Σ_i rank of the class
   vectors; NP-hard in general, not a matroid union/intersection/parity problem), solved exactly here by splitting the delivery matroid into components (208 / 28 / 14 elements plus 13 coloops),
   exhaustive span-tuple DP on the small ones (16 and 9 pivots) and, on the 208, an exact block DP with a coupling-assignment lower bound and an exhaustive search (minimum sum-rank 121, so 87 pivots;
   120 shown infeasible): 87 + 16 + 9 = 112. The annealing plateau (14 of 16 restarts at 112, never 113) is therefore optimal. Priced by the model, a rank-1 pivot is worth ≈ +0.033% of c,
   so the pivot count on R715 is exhausted within this format (177 would have been ≈ +2.9%; it is not reachable; the donor choice among 112-pivot selections still moves c, README §3).
   *Scope:* the 177 and 586 are valid but loose scoped bounds; the 177 does not cover non-coordinate entrances. Upstream `kernel()` itself accepts any flat; there all 706 helpers qualify and the same argument
   gives only 706 − 120 = 586, in a format this package does not verify (it needs coordinate residual isometries). The exact 112 is a statement about the same coordinate, one-class-per-donor model;
   entrances at arbitrary root lines were only searched.
   *Follow-up:* the same exact method gives 101 pivots on the R687 read-then-climb word (100 after the parity rule); to be reported in a follow-up PR.
3. **The method:** `select_kernel.py` anneals the class assignment on the exact objective Σ rank (self-contained xorshift64*, reproducible from a seed),
   `kernel_from_selection.py` builds the word with #443's kernel unchanged. Pinned: `--seed 3 --iters 150000`.
4. Honest size: by kernel choice alone, without retiming or reordering, the first 112-pivot selection (c = 1.295564·10⁻³) landed, in κ, within 0.003% of #473 as first posted (1.293922·10⁻³);
   the shipped best-of-eight seed was 0.027% above that. #473 has since been updated (1.295630·10⁻³) and is 0.108% above this PR. This is selection tuning, not a ≥ 1% result.

**Verification** (`python -B research/e8-r715-kernel-cap/verify.py /abs/out [--light]`; CI workflow `e8-r715-kernel-cap`): LIGHT (about two minutes) checks integrity and
pins, recomputes the ceiling analysis from the pinned R715 word, **recomputes the exact pivot maximum and asserts 112**, checks the selection against #443's exact kernel conditions plus the F₂ response relation and the coordinate-flat condition,
rebuilds the kernel word (replay, interface) and the mixed word and compares them, checks the width rule, re-solves the hosting (CP-SAT) and prices it with the
exact engine, and runs the screen composition with #458's pinned endpoint. FULL adds the seeded search, #443's regressions, the relaxed all-column checker,
C++ cohort legality and formal columns at five and eleven stages, mixing mutants, Gram, eleven-stage template/audits, **hosting selection rediscovered with HiGHS and
required equal**, hosted audit, assembly, the pivot-count scan, #458's complex supplier from scratch, and the exact composition (two moment engines per side, six
bootstrap levels, all 47 strict outer inequalities, next-grid / zero-η / zero-β / unit-β rejection).

**Review points**
- The ceiling's proof (items 1–4 of README §2) is elementary. The new claim is the exact maximum 112: its certificate is the code in `code/exact_pivots.py` (component split, block DP,
  coupling lower bound, exhaustive search), rerun in LIGHT; please review that code and the min-sum-rank formulation of README §2 items 2–3 it relies on.
- The seed choice among equal pivot counts is an exact-priced selection (c between 1.295564 and 1.295911·10⁻³ across eight seeds).
- Inherited and unchanged: #450's Lemma M (bit target mixing, chained receivers), #458's paid adapters, the R715 hierarchy and its carrier bound (#463).

This adds `research/tensor-nonroot-pairs`, an offline source-bound finite construction with conditional kappa = **0.001301970637653655**, approximately **0.3456% above PR473 at 4bea72f5cfa700dba4556bdb5d2761d7577b7a6c**. It uses an explicit GL cover and the inherited compiler/analytic contracts; it is not an unconditional integer-multiplication theorem or a Lean certificate.

## New mechanism

The old kernel search intersected sets of named E8 roots. We instead intersect their actual rational spans. This exposes 56 auxiliary directions of the form e_i +/- e_j that were invisible to that representation. The selected construction adds 22 response-kernel pivots on top of the updated rank139 basis and response retiming. Their simultaneous source-bound word changes the local paid histogram by +84 rank1 and -53 rank2; all 955 arbitrary-dirty columns and 22 omission controls pass.

These new entrance lines need non-coordinate residual routes. Two copies have an explicit rational orthogonal 16-by-16 normalization: their intact rank7 residual projectors are orthogonal and sum to a rank14 coordinate projector. We place each pair inside ONE owner family, with two restored spectator directions. No logical residual is split across different physical families. Full 78-column owner maps include the actual port/window basis, the entrance directions, placement and inverse; matching dimensions alone is not accepted.

The physical program contains 88 complete local invocations, 62,920 whole residual occurrences,968 paired blocks and 1,733,496 emitted events, including 23,040 bridge updates. All costs are recomputed from this one program; gains from different proposals are never added numerically.

## Exact price and scope

- Final kappa: 1301970637653655 / 10^18.
- Bit saving: see the exact rational bracket in EXPECTED.json; approximately 0.001303667975.
- Unchanged complex saving: 1305231506267591 / 10^18.
- Live stock 9600, physical stock 9609, rank mass 745536, deficit 3264.
- Physical prefix 1684 bits, charged 1728.
- Concrete route 224 elementary factors per direction, conservatively charged 512.
- PR490 GL-cover sharp bad-class charge and enlarged row allowance 28416 are used. The fixed-q weighted-routing constant B_GL stays explicit in the symbolic bootstrap cutoff.

This does not claim to beat PR480's higher cross-copy headline. That claim retains the disputed operator admission discussed in PR448/451; no such split is used here. The construction also does not achieve the larger campaign target.

## Reproduction and validation

    python -B research/tensor-nonroot-pairs/verify.py /absolute/new/output

Python3.11+, SymPy, C++17 and Boost are required. Set CXX/BOOST_INCLUDE if necessary. No network, annealer or discovery optimizer is required. Default rebuilds both suppliers. `--complex-output` accepts only the exact completed complex receipt and 87 implementation/17 output hashes pinned in the package; any reuse is explicitly reported.

Checks include source reconstruction, fresh native legality and five-/eleven-stage columns, 1,019 positive Gram frames, exact auxiliary-line decoder,22 omitted-correction controls, rational route/inverse/projector/factor controls, actual full-matrix owner injection, complete chronological emission, independently reconstructed physical-family row invoice, two rational moment engines, six bootstrap rounds and 47 strict inequalities with next-grid/degenerate-parameter controls. VALIDATION.json and release receipts specify the packaged run; finite verification does not discharge the inherited all-size contracts.

Two representation fixes are explicit and source-bound: the decoder's full-frame mask uses 176 lines while retaining 120 semantic ports, and half-inner-products remain rational instead of being floored. The general integer-basis native auditor is unchanged.

## Direct credits

- **PR473**: updated rank139 basis exchanges, exact nested response source and whole-owner packing framework.
- **PR483**, **PR478**, **PR476**: response cancellation, nested flags and target-factor lineage retained in the base word.
- **PR485**: the scoped coordinate-kernel analysis motivated searching actual geometric intersections rather than named roots.
- **PR490**: fixed-GL whole-owner transport, sharp fallback, row28416 and explicit routing cutoff.
- **PR470**, **PR472**, **PR463**, **PR443**: R715 word, retiming, shared-response construction and checked local interfaces.
- **PR471**, **PR458**: unchanged complex supplier, full-nine-axis normalization, paid wrappers and same-owner spectator handling.
- **PR442**, **PR451**, **PR465**: hosting/compressed-stage infrastructure and fallback-accounting lineage.

The immutable-source retiming is reused from our earlier unpublished tensor-syndrome-portfolio package and adapted to the new basis; we do not claim to have invented it again. Classical rational linear algebra, two-square/Hadamard normalization and quaternion four-square identities underlie the new routing. Existing license and source notices are retained.

## Saved research for future work

The package includes the general four-copy rational hosting proof, exact two-copy witnesses, the auxiliary-intersection method, independent composition review, and the tested complex partial-response/centre-lattice routes with their paid-cost limitations. PR484's larger complex-supplier proposal was studied but is not silently included in this exponent. Overlapping candidate counts, optimistic profiles and uncompleted routes are explicitly separated from the achieved construction. Nothing was published by the assistant.

**No κ claim.** These are research notes on the E8 unit geometry and on supplier and outer levers. Everything is in `research/e8-decoder-floors-and-cold14-notes/`: one `README.md` with 16 sections, plus a package per section. Each package has its scripts and logs, and most have a `verify.sh` with expected outputs. SAT results have no proof logs unless stated otherwise.

## Headline results

**Gaussian E8 is nearly closed as an E8 replacement.** The unit is E8 over ℤ[i]: 60 lines, window 4. A decoder that beats real E8 needs Theorem-C cost ≤ 42. Proven:
- every decoder costs ≥ 40, and ≥ max(40, 60 − c) for c totals (§10, §15);
- c = 15 costs exactly 60 (§13);
- c ≤ 18 is excluded (§14, §15);
- c = 19 is excluded (§16, MIP bounds).

What remains is **20 ≤ c ≤ 42**: c = 20 is partly done, and c ≥ 21 has an F2 2×2-support route.

**The other E8 replacements lose to E8.**
- Eisenstein (Witting, 40 lines) and Hurwitz E8 cost ≥ v over every decoder (§10).
- Real ADE systems other than E8, the triple family, Lorentzian I_{11,1}/I_{13,1} and K12 have higher ceilings in some cases, but lose once helper costs are counted (§1, §4, §5, §7).

**E8's own decoder floors are tight.** Theorem C equals the star floor: 72 / 63 / 64 for P120 / P111 / P112. The P111 decoder is unique, and deeper punctures, mixed ports and asymmetric sinks are all worse (§2).

**"No new kappa" construction savings cannot move κ.** κ depends only on the paid rank profile and the live stock; ADD and primitive counts enter only slack admission checks (§8).

**Supplier local-edit searches are exhausted on recent words:**
- fusions and triangle slots on the X54 words (§9);
- helper-donor cold kernels on #1319 (§11);
- an extended census on the 566 + 554 T74 word, which also explains why §11 missed those kernels (§12).

## Section index
| § | Topic | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Real ADE root systems as units | only E8 viable (E6 row corrected, per #630) |
| 2 | E8 decoder floors | Theorem C = star (72/63/64); P111 unique; no cheaper variants |
| 3 | #615/#617 levers | e2 ends infeasible; owner map LP-optimal (historical) |
| 4 | E8 over ℤ[i], ℤ[ω], Hurwitz; K12 | minrank = v/w, so x = 1 under the star premise |
| 5 | Triple and Lorentzian families | higher X*, lose after a calibrated helper model |
| 6 | Dispatch and cold-end pricing (#639 lineage) | ck removal +1.08e-7 b; dim-7 factored ends positive |
| 7 | I_{11,1} / I_{13,1} punctures and helpers | no improving puncture; no 4-frame partition |
| 8 | Why "no new kappa" savings are zero | κ = f(paid profile, W) |
| 9 | Fusion and slot search on the fused X54 words | 0 gains; idle-overlay PRs noted as withdrawn |
| 10 | Extension-ring floors over all decoders | Eisenstein and Hurwitz excluded; Gaussian ≥ 40 |
| 11 | Cold-kernel census on the #1319 word | 0 gains (scope limited, see §12) |
| 12 | Supplier census on the 566 + 554 T74 word | why §11 missed them; extended families give 0 gains |
| 13 | Gaussian, 15 totals | cost exactly 60 (rank-drop; 3 flat orbits; 1,500-flat sweep) |
| 14 | Gaussian, 16 totals | cost ≥ 43 (level tables) |
| 15 | Gaussian, all c | cost ≥ max(40, 60 − c); c = 18 excluded (parity) |
| 16 | Gaussian, 19–20 totals | μ-packing theorem; c = 19 excluded; c = 20 partial |

## Open problems
- Gaussian E8 at 20 ≤ c ≤ 42.
- Supplier gains outside B-local kernels: the A stage and the parent/centre interface.

Earlier versions of this description covered only §1–§3. Related work: #630, #631, #634, #703, #738, #767, #801, #888, #1957, #2066.

PR628's binary dirty commutator has quadratic factor-call growth and an executable phase-alias admission defect. This contribution adds a subquadratic multiway echo, a one-line alias guard, an exact full-transform/bit integration experiment, and bit-sharing cost gates that include physical owner restoration. The integration works functionally, but its complete recursive bill rejects this direct adapter as a route to larger κ. This is a construction refinement, executable repair and scoped negative research result.

### Local construction and verifier repair

The multiway echo composes noncommuting factor shears while restoring arbitrary borrowed data. Fixed fanout 8 reduces the leaf-call exponent from 2 to approximately 1.602452 with O(log n) borrowed arrays. At 512 factors the exact count falls from 262,144 to 21,952, using 21 arrays instead of 9. The flat variant takes 4n−4 calls and n−1 arrays. The complete inherited error recurrence is included; this is a classical local primitive, not an admitted multiplication supplier.

At pinned PR628, `phases is x` passes admission even though phases must remain read-only. For `x=phases=[1,1]`, outer b=1/4 and eight fractional bits, execution returns x=[1,15/16]. The submitted patch rejects source/target/scratch phase aliases before mutation. Replay applies the actual patch to the pinned Git source. More precision does not repair this exact counterexample.

### Full-transform and bit integration

`research/dirty-echo-integration/` implements:

- An all-role complex adapter and Boolean address-chunk interchange, including outputs on every role borrowed during execution.
- Complete normalized synthetic Fourier transforms over C[y]/(y^r+1), stored bit-reversed frequency order, signed monomial twiddles, opposite transforms and correctly normalized convolution.
- Independent exact references, instruction/interface corruption controls, source pins and deterministic evidence.

Three shears per pair complete the all-role adapter. Even granting one recursive child per additive leaf and making routing, phases, storage, preparation and precision free, its moment is `3 N(n)/(2 n^(1-b))`. Since `N(n) >= 4n-4`, its moment at saving zero is at least `6-6/n >= 3`. This rejects **this adapter's** bill for every nonnegative saving; it is not a lower bound for other integrations or suppliers.

Two exact counterexamples prevent silently substituting different operators: replacing the triangular Newton factor by its cyclic counterpart fails at radix 4, with a rank-r−1 boundary correction; the radix-3 cyclic kernel is singular on a length-5 cycle over GF(4). The latter rules out the unrestricted finite-field analogue, not restricted lengths or Boolean address permutations.

At κ=0.01, both retained supplier savings must exceed 1/99. With unchanged widths and volumes, uniform reductions of all paid terms would need to exceed approximately 2.70% for pinned #589 and 2.47% for pinned #659. These are exact-moment diagnostic targets, not feasible fractional deletions or replacement suppliers. No κ gain is attributed to the echo integration.

### Bit sharing priced before construction

`research/bit-role-sharing-budget/` extracts the actual PR589 local paid profile and all 661 Boolean columns, retains the complete frozen hosting remainder and fallback, and compares role-sharing budgets at the necessary bit saving 1/99 for κ=0.01.

- Equal-call pooling saves dispatches but not volume-weighted recursive work. A fixed-address-permutation rank argument also excludes fewer queried role volumes under arbitrary invertible XOR row charts and restored private dirt. Different address-dependent charts and native primitives are outside this model.
- Even ideal rank-8 consolidation of every local rank unit fails the target. Making all retained-total copies free still fails. The corresponding bit-only outer ceilings are below 0.002644610326897 and 0.007315906873875; neither is an achieved supplier.
- With the original rank mass and boundary remainder, cap 55 fails and cap 56 is the first passing relaxation. A hypothetical integer rank-57 invoice allows 431 extra rank-1 repair calls globally and needs over 98.48% of local rank mass fused. The eight-stage interpretation applies only to one port's active spaces; cross-port sharing has a larger span.
- A different arithmetic target is ideal rank-8 consolidation plus 100 **net paid rank units** removed per invocation after hosting: 99 fails, 100 passes. This is not achieved by simply deleting helpers or XORs.

No replacement supplier was built: the simple sharing classes fail even under favorable complete-cost bounds, and the passing high-rank/mass-reduction targets still lack an operator and hosting plan. No new κ is claimed. The independent positive-atanh engine reproduces the current bit root and agrees with the inherited Mercator engine on 133 complete invoices. Normal/optimized evidence is byte-identical; 108 small coded-query programs, 384 positive-control basis columns, source/scatter/expected-evidence mutations and a relocated minimal replay are checked.

Standalone command: `sh research/bit-role-sharing-budget/replay.sh /tmp/bit-role-sharing-budget`. Expected final line: `PASS_BIT_ROLE_SHARING_REPLAY`. The combined command below now includes this screen. Final overlap review through #716 distinguishes #705/#708/#714/#715; no new pinned coordination issue was found.

### Concrete bit-sharing candidate and physical hosting gate

`research/bit-sharing-hosting-gate/` follows the 100-net-unit arithmetic target with an exact scalar candidate and a source-bound reconstruction of all **126,432** frozen helper reservations. Neither candidate is admitted as a supplier.

- The nine-stage source-bank masks have one exact dependence: the last source is the XOR of the preceding eight. Nine running accumulators per replica can therefore share the source part of the retained decoder totals at the scalar level. The actual snapshots have rank-nine dirty contamination. The proposed owned-storage plan adds 288 persistent rows and nine temporary rows; source extraction, copy, clear and XOR costs are listed. ADDRESS-chart alignment is still unproved. Even gifting it, the maximum COPY credit is only **7 rank units per invocation**, with target moment 1.026605906228685.
- A hypothetical free producer eliminating 13 helper paths removes **104 local rank units**, but the explicit idle owners must complete all 104 vacated directions: **zero net credit**. The new complete profile is priced after coalescing those directions at the owners' original boundaries. Every one of the 439 single-helper eliminations has the same mass conservation. These favorable screens do not assert a replacement producer exists.
- The previous 100-unit screen granted rank-8 consolidation everywhere. Keeping the 222 rank-7 data climbs makes 100 and 101 fail; **102 first passes that narrower relaxation**. More fundamentally, under the current data/cover boundary identity, even zero COPY cost saves only 63 per invocation. Reaching 100 requires a changed boundary term.
- A scope control changes the hosting remainder: free elimination of all helper work plus perfect data consolidation still fails with COPY retained, but passes if COPY is also granted free. Thus 100 is not a universal necessary condition for other suppliers; the complete moment remains decisive.

The package verifies all 888 source-bank columns, retained source/dirty ranks and reflected copy forms, reconstructs chronological windows and disjoint owners independently of the parent allocator, and compares **449 complete invoices with two exact rational engines**. Normal, optimized and relocated minimal replays agree; six ownership/admission controls plus source/receipt corruption controls are rejected. For orthogonal P and Q, incoming source/target frames P/Q and outgoing Q-perp/P-perp give the exact local operator with diagonal D_(I-P-Q) and off-diagonal D_I. A different, **unrealized local word** with rank(Q)=2 would have rank-five data climbs. Charging every local rank unit as its own rank-one child gives moment 0.9947928245644905 at c=1/99+10^-9 and conditional net saving 197 1/3 units per invocation. Adding 31 rank-one repair children per invocation still passes at 0.9999126541717095, with net saving 166 1/3; 32 fails the rate test. These are conditional construction targets, not achieved improvements.

The actual PR589 scalar order cannot realize the new endpoints by monotone re-framing: its least frame closure forces all 111 sources to full rank eight during cleanup. A new local source/read/restoration topology is required. The Gaussian appendix separately shows that the reported 80-rational-rank COPY floor, under the stated B_K slot model, bounds every stage count below c=0.0078; it does not re-prove that external floor or exclude other delivery models.

Standalone: `sh research/bit-paired-boundary-gate/replay.sh /tmp/paired-boundary-new-output`. Normal and optimized evidence agree; relocated minimal replay, source/receipt corruption controls, owner timing/collision controls, two exact price engines and selected-record integrity pass. The combined driver includes this package; its unchanged older stages were not repeated in this increment. The full goal remains unachieved: no paired local supplier, finite controller admission or new kappa is claimed. Final overlap metadata was checked through #802, including #791/#801 and the updated #717.

```

Completed checks include 300 alias-repair differential cases and 19 early rejections; 72 ideal echo cases, 744 rounded comparisons, 120 dense inverse/error checks and 62 aliases; 168 complex adapter basis cases, 11,616 symbolic Boolean rows, six complete transform/convolution configurations, 40 transform basis columns, 59 signed rotations, 12 integration corruption controls and six wrong-normalization controls. Functional evidence agrees under isolated optimized Python. Relocated minimal replay passes; altered source pins and expected evidence fail. Selected-record integrity and staged whitespace checks pass. The inherited full bit circuit, root-wide suite, remote CI and proof-assistant verification are not claimed.

Main base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. Integration continuation base: `0e35f56cab3cae1eb0a99447135569d687c5695a`. PR669 proves the sharp puncture threshold for target-local stars and explicitly leaves punctured decoders using arbitrary off-target stars open. This **research note / scoped negative result** closes that larger scalar class: for every power-of-two k >= 2 and p >= k, decoding one retained target requires exactly **2(p-k)+1** deleted ports. **No new kappa or paid supplier is claimed.**

The written elementary proof establishes the stronger identity d(C_{p,k}) = 2(p-k+1) for the global degree-<k star evaluation code, including the empty star, for every k >= 2. It uses generalized-cube parity, an even-face lemma and restriction induction. At a power-of-two k, permitted target overlap-class corrections add no functions to that code. The attaining witness uses one nonempty (k-1)-star.

A ten-star p=5,k=4 example reaches the same threshold while all 16 target intersection cells survive. Thus PR669's **minimum threshold** extends globally, while its **local cell feasibility criterion** does not. Exact elimination checks local infeasibility for this example.

Changes are limited to research/global-star-puncture/ and one scoped workflow. The accepted conditional kappa remains 51110230636731/31250000000000000; selected-result, existing suppliers, generators and upstream/ are unchanged.

### Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/global-star-puncture/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_GLOBAL_STAR_PUNCTURE: sharp deletion thresholds 3/5; 2 independent F2 engines; 960 correction rows; 12 negative controls`.

The complete deterministic receipt is compared on every run. A packed row-space quotient and a separately written list-RREF/nullspace implementation agree on 80/240-port domains, ranks 65/155 and distances 4/6. All 28,680 pair syndromes in the second domain are distinct. Coverage also includes all 38,344 codewords in seven small domains, exhaustive even-face support checks in dimensions 1–4, valid generalized-face cubes, and a non-power-of-two positive escape control. Finite replay supports the written proof; it is not a formal proof of the multiplication theorem.

The theorem concerns one specified retained target, arbitrary global proper-star coefficients and fixed coefficients within each overlap class. ## Change and mathematical scope

**Status: research note with a finite circuit construction and exact verification. No new κ.** The selected certificate, its κ (`51110230636731/31250000000000000`) and `upstream/` are unchanged. All files are new, under `research/r420-block9-factorization/`.

In eumemic's #543 R420 bit word, phase-B block 9 is the 38-XOR slice `B[559:597]` at frame 551 (rational rank four), on the twelve source registers `8, 13, 33, 39, 42, 47, 80, 85, 88, 94, 114, 119`. This PR replaces it with 24 XORs. Regenerating the literal reverse cleanup saves 14 more, at the rank-eight full frame. D, A, the scatter, the retained totals and every other B gate are unchanged.

| Quantity | Original | Replacement |
|---|---:|---:|
| Block 9 XORs | 38 | 24 |
| Literal cleanup gate records | 2,661 | 2,647 |
| Complete native scalar ADDs | 26,916 | 26,888 |
| Local reverse positive prefix bound | 2,270,064 | 2,234,964 |
| Local forward positive prefix bound | 144,651 | 144,651 |
| Paid rank mass | 5,112 | 5,112 |

- **Exact block identity.** Write `T_ab = I + e_a e_b^T`. The old and new chronological gate lists have the same positive integer transfer matrix, so block 9 computes the same linear map over every commutative ring, F2 included, on arbitrary register contents. The signed inverse is also identical, and the ordered physical output assignment is kept. The complete dirty-restored word is certified over F2; its defining endpoint is not claimed over the integers.
- **Positive bounds do not grow.** The positive reverse transfer is entrywise no larger, with 22 strict entries. Block followed by positive reverse improves 102 entries, and its unit-input maximum falls from 973 to 137. The unchanged exterior operations are monotone on nonnegative bounds, so the domination carries through the whole word and no prefix bound increases. The five-stage payload stays at 100 bits and the nine-stage charge at 192 bits.
- **No hidden cost.** The change adds no helper, source access, copy, frame change or recursive child. Every register keeps its frame path, and the paid histogram `{1:1320, 2:1440, 4:60, 5:120, 8:9}` is unchanged. The interface is #543's original H1–H5, including literal cleanup reversal (H4).
- **Search.** A seeded walk factors the block's 12-by-12 transfer matrix from both ends: subtracting a dominated row removes a final gate, subtracting a column removes a first gate, and entries stay nonnegative. With OS seed 19 it ran a fixed 2,000 trials. 372 reached the identity, 236 of those had a dominated positive reverse, and the best has 24 gates. 24 is not claimed minimal.

**Predecessor work.** Details and pins are in the README and SOURCES.json.
- eumemic's #543, reviewed at `2065fe4f72a914d907f1046603f5a36f17018535`, supplies the R420 word, source plan, integer norm objective, interleaved interface and exact checker, building on #493.
- The exporter, checker and pricing lineage is credited in the README: Dylan Crow (#370 word and exporter), DaysSky (bridged cohort checker), DreamingOfClouds (#503/#510 and #463 nine-stage pricing), Zhihao Chen (#425 interface), Chafik Boukhalfa (common-label and hosting/emitter work), and the cumulative authors in the selected maintainer review.
- #661 (yuj1r0) proves the R420 phase-B frames moment-optimal at fixed gate order and excludes resynthesis. This PR changes the gate list instead of reopening that class.

**Open obligations.**
- Build the globally hosted owner program, physical invoice and outer assembly for the changed word, and update the supplier bindings. In the nine-stage invoice's scalar term, `9 * 32 * local_additions + bridge_additions`, the local saving would remove 8,064 ADDs; nothing hosted is regenerated here.
- Settle whether 24 gates is minimal for this block.
- Discharge the inherited all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-basis realization, pooled hosting, normalized residual, precision/tape/exact-recovery and analytic-transfer assumptions.

No κ change follows from the local count: the recursive profile and rounded prefix budgets are unchanged, and the selected assembly is complex-bound.

[Research note and proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/README.md), [frozen circuit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/CANDIDATE.json), [certificate](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/CERTIFICATE.json), [source pins](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/SOURCES.json), [validation record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/VALIDATION.json), [verifier](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/verify.py) and [search](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/search.py).

**Overlap.** The pre-submission refresh at 05:31 UTC on 13 October searched the titles and bodies of the 320 most recent PRs (#462–#782, all states) and read every R420 circuit PR among them; none changes block 9's gates. `main` is still at base `66849e1`, so no merged change touches the word. #670 (yongjae321) and #674 (x0hu) resynthesize blocks 3 and 5, by local F2 rewrites and explicit sum sharing. #688 (Ali Romman) composes those two, and #681 (alluri-ritual) consolidates #688 with phase-A, D, decoder and complex-supplier work; none of the four touches block 9, and no composition with them is certified here. The one direct interaction is #754 (namredips), which keeps B fixed and rewrites four-wire cleanup windows under a semantic H4′. Two of its 101 windows, `[120,124)` and `[126,130)` of the expanded original cleanup (one XOR each), lie inside block 9's reversed segment `[120,158)`, which this PR replaces wholesale, so the two savings are not additive. #710's conjugation lies outside that segment, and #691 (mtpsl) applies the same forward-equality and reverse-domination test to phase-A quad 13. #686, #694, #713, #716, #733, #742, #759 and #774 change the frame-zero compensation D, and #708, #748 and #753 change the phase-A decoder totals; each saves more than 28 ADDs. This PR is the only change to block 9, and unlike several of those D and decoder changes it raises no positive prefix bound.

## Validation

From the repository root, with Python 3.11+, a C++17 compiler and Boost headers (no Python packages):

```sh
python3 -B research/r420-block9-factorization/verify.py
```

Expected final line:

```text
PASS_R420_BLOCK9_FACTORIZATION gates=38->24 native_adds=26916->26888 columns=660/900/1380/1620 rank_mass=5112
```

The driver writes the rebuilt word, exported records, checker receipts and logs to a fresh directory under `build/`, and compares every proof-relevant field with CERTIFICATE.json. It compares regenerated gzip output by canonical decompressed JSON. The lane's run passed on Linux x86-64 with Python 3.12.3 and GCC 13.3.0.

- **Finite checks.**
  - Exact integer transfer, signed inverse and entrywise positive-bound comparisons for the block, in unbounded Python integers.
  - #543's own E8 label, rational-frame, all-column and H1–H5 checks on both complete words.
  - A separate standard-library interpreter replays all 660 dirty-input columns one at a time in both orientations, and reconstructs every exported MOVE/ADD/COPY/ERASE record, frame path, paid profile and positive prefix. It imports no predecessor checker or search code.
  - The unchanged C++ legality checker and five-, nine- and eleven-stage column checkers run on both words: 900, 1,380 and 1,620 physical columns, with 6, 18 and 24 omitted-bridge controls per word. The C++ and Python prefix and profile results must agree.
  - The checker rejects all 15 new negative controls. They include an integer-correct 25-gate factorization with a worse positive reverse, and a stale literal cleanup that passes the F2 endpoint replay but fails H4.
- **Proof arguments.** Equality over every commutative ring follows from the equal integer transfer matrices. The README gives the written argument that reverse domination propagates through the monotone exterior to every prefix of the whole word; the finite prefix replays agree with it but do not replace it.
- **Search reproduction.** `python3 -B research/r420-block9-factorization/search.py --seed 19 --trials 2000 --output NEW-candidate.json` regenerates the frozen candidate in the recorded environment. Verification neither imports the search nor trusts its trace.
- **Repository checks.** `make selected-record-check` passes: `PASS selected record, exact kappa, original source inventory and proof supplement: 51110230636731/31250000000000000`. `git diff --check` is clean, and no existing file or `upstream/` byte changes. The verifier above was re-run on the submitted commit.
- **Not claimed.** This is not a formal verification of the multiplication theorem, not a hosted, invoice or outer-assembly replay, and not a full repository suite, Linux CI or Lean pass. No composition with a concurrent PR is certified, and 24 gates is not claimed minimal.

Sprint: bit-supplier track, OS seed 19. The claim and its result update are recorded locally. Submitted by @commdata2338 with substantial AI assistance, under Apache-2.0: OpenAI Codex (GPT-6-Astra) wrote the analysis, proof and checker, and Claude Code packaged the submission. No independent human peer review is claimed.

## Change and mathematical scope

**Status: research construction with exact verification. No new κ.** The selected certificate, its κ (`51110230636731/31250000000000000`) and `upstream/` are unchanged. All files are new, under `research/r420-target-compensation/`.

eumemic's #543 R420 bit word implements its frame-zero dirty-helper compensation D, `y <- y + K s` for a fixed binary 120-by-420 matrix `K`, with 19,922 XORs. This PR factors `K` through a reversible target basis. D first applies 205 target transvections `y[a] ^= y[b]`, whose product is `E`. It then adds helpers along the 11,633 nonzero entries of `R = E K`, and finally repeats the 205 transvections in reverse order. Over F2 the result is `E^-1 (E y + R s) = y + K s` for arbitrary incoming targets and helpers. D never writes a helper or a source and needs no workspace.

| Quantity | #543 | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| D XORs (entrance + helper injections + exit) | 19,922 | 12,043 (205 + 11,633 + 205) |
| Complete native word, XORs | 26,916 | 19,037 |
| Hosted instructions, 288 local calls | 8,603,712 | 6,334,560 |
| Forward / reverse positive bounds F / B | 144,651 / 2,270,064 | 144,651 / 4,409,580 |
| Local payload `64 F^3 B^2`, bits (cap 104) | 100 | 102 |
| Nine-stage prefix `2^18 F^5 B^4` / charge, bits | 189 / 192 | 192 / 192 |
| Two-level coefficient / charge, bits | 416 / 512 | 424 / 512 |

- **Unchanged.** Only D changes. The 420 helpers, the nine COPY/ERASE pairs, every register's frame path, the paid profile `{1:1320, 2:1440, 4:60, 5:120, 8:9}` with rank mass 5,112, and the recursive children stay as they are. The bit lower bound and the selected κ reproduce exactly.
- **Prefix.** The reverse bound grows. The search admitted a row step only if F stayed at most 144,651 and B at most 4,409,638, the largest B with `2^18 F^5 B^4 < 2^192`, so the existing 192-bit nine-stage and 512-bit two-level charges still hold. The unrounded invoice coefficient increases. The claim is fewer instructions under unchanged charges, not a measured speedup.
- **Changed hypothesis.** The new D breaks #543's gate-local H2, under which D gates read only helpers, and #543's direct `K_equals_D` extraction no longer applies. The verifier records both predicates as false and keeps every other H1–H5 check. In their place, README.md proves a semantic D-boundary lemma: D runs at frame zero and implements exactly `(x, y, s) -> (x, y + K s, s)`, so the unchanged remainder of the word sees identical values and frames. The verifier checks that boundary on all 660 symbolic columns.
- **Search.** OS seed 18 chose this object (`18 mod 3 = 0` among three candidates). At each step a greedy pass scored every ordered pair of target rows, kept only steps that passed an exact incremental prefix check, and broke ties with the seed. It stopped after 205 steps and 2,941,680 pair evaluations, when no admissible positive-gain pair remained; the cap was 1,000 steps. An unrestricted control with the same seed reached 10,384 D XORs but needed 201 nine-stage bits and broke the 104-bit payload cap, so it is kept only as a rejected control. 12,043 is not claimed optimal.

**Predecessor work.** Details and pins for 39 source files are in README.md and SOURCES.json.
- eumemic's #543, reviewed at `2065fe4f72a914d907f1046603f5a36f17018535` and building on #493, supplies the word, the compensation matrix, the interleaved interface and the checker this package reuses.
- Credit carried from #543's lineage: Dylan Crow (E8 word, record and checker lineage), DreamingOfClouds (#503/#510, generalized nine-stage accounting), DaysSky (bridged columns, whole-call hosting), Zhihao Chen (mutable-source/common-label and compressed geometry) and Chafik Boukhalfa (physical routes, templates and audits). Chafik Boukhalfa's selected #626 supplies the complex lower bound that the hosted replay cites.
- Dugongue's #476 and #478 used the reversible donor-receiver target identity on R715 phase B. Each transvection pair here is that identity, applied to the compensation.
- Mikhail R. Gadelha's concurrent #686 published the semantic D-boundary substitution first. This PR claims no priority for it or for basis factoring.

**Open obligations.**
- A maintainer must accept the semantic D-boundary lemma in place of the gate-local H2 and update the supplier's source bindings.
- B sits 58 below the nine-stage cutoff, so combining this D with any change that raises F or B needs a fresh prefix recount.
- The all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-basis realization, pooled hosting, normalized residual, precision/tape recovery and analytic-transfer assumptions remain inherited.

[Research note and proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/README.md), [frozen recipe](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/candidate.json), [certificate](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/CERTIFICATE.json), [hosted certificate](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/HOSTED-CERTIFICATE.json), [source pins](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/SOURCES.json), [validation record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/VALIDATION.json), [seed, search and overlap record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/RESEARCH.json), [verifier](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/verify.py) and [search](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/search.py).

**Overlap.** No coordination issue exists; the only open issue, #650, asks about Discussions. The circuit was nominated and frozen locally before any concurrent D PR was read (RESEARCH.json records the freeze at 04:19 UTC on 13 October), and nothing from those PRs is imported. The package README records the overlap as of 04:25 UTC, when only #686 and #694 had appeared. A refresh between 05:28 and 05:37 UTC searched PR titles and bodies through #788 and read every PR among them that changes D. `main` is still `66849e1`, so nothing on D has merged. Many open PRs now change this D, and two reach lower counts:

| PR | Basis and recipe class | D XORs | Native XORs | Nine-stage bits |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| This PR | target; 205 successive steps | 12,043 | 19,037 | 192 |
| #686 | helper; one pair | 19,814 | 26,808 | 189 |
| #694 | helper; 201 disjoint pairs | 12,988 | 19,982 | 192 |
| #713 | target; 57 disjoint pairs | 16,772 | 23,766 | 191 |
| #716 | target; 60 disjoint pairs, optimal among disjoint pairs | 16,672 | 23,666 | 191 |
| #742 | target; shared donors | 16,634 | 23,628 | 192 |
| #759 | target; rooted forest | 15,138 | 22,132 | 197 |
| #774 | target; forest with optimized cuts | 15,025 | 22,019 | 197 |
| #733 | #694's helper basis, then 57 target pairs | 11,554 | 18,548 | 195 |
| #681 | #694's helper basis, then 56 target pairs, in a six-PR consolidation | 11,562 | 18,378 | 196 |

The last column applies this package's nine-stage formula to each PR's reported F and B. The other D PRs check the local payload against 2^104 and leave the hosted prefix to integration; #681 reports 196 bits itself, and the formula reproduces it. #681's native count includes its phase-A, phase-B and decoder changes.

- **Lower counts.** Scott Woolsey Biggart's #733 and the D stage of Alluri's #681 use 489 and 481 fewer D XORs than this PR. Both exceed the 192-bit nine-stage charge: #681 raises its allocation to 256 bits and replays the hosted invoice at that charge, and #733 leaves global invoices open. This PR does not settle whether their extra savings are worth the larger allocation.

**Update: current selected word (#741).** Rebased on main after #741 merged. I gave CP-SAT PR699's SW4 word (`d232183f…`), using the admissible model with the audit's hpe cone caps and fixed tail frames. In 27 s it returned `OPTIMAL` with exactly #741's profile `{1:2556,2:334,3:430,4:194,5:56,8:8}`, so the solver rediscovers #741's gain without guidance. `check_sw4.py` applies #741's recipe and reproduces its pinned output hash `e7804702…`. The LP optimum over all frame assignments then equals #741's weight: 18155.950422 linear and 18219.665540 exact-root at #741's complex root, with gaps under 1e-9. So **no frame-only change of the selected word can raise κ**; PR699's frame slack (6.90 units) is exactly what #741 recovered. Six commuting-reorder restarts on #741, each re-solved by the LP, gave no gain. The receipt is `RESULT-SW4.json`. This work does not touch the R420/R439 bit or E8 lines (#789/#790/#792, #765/#767/#770).

**Negative result, scoped. No κ change.** By Rohan Guliani (@Rohansguliani), with substantial AI assistance (an AI coding agent wrote the search code and ran the experiments).

The complex side binds the selected κ. In the 64 jp8 calls, unit climbs make up 160,768 of the 181,659 rank-1 children. Paid children are exactly the frame climbs that `hpe_audit_and_transport.py::climb` counts, and the scalar program never reads frames. So I treated every A/B/tail gate frame of the selected provider words as a variable and searched all of them exactly.

**Result.** For #626's `jp8` and `ck` words (content hashes pinned in `complex-k492-owner-repair/data/SPEC.json`, rebuilt fresh by the package's `verify.py`), the paid profile is optimal over every frame assignment of the fixed gate sequence:

| word | gates | input weight | LP optimum (HiGHS) | CP-SAT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| jp8 | 4471 | 18475.029780700 | 18475.029780701 | OPTIMAL, same value |
| ck | 4507 | 18568.580702034 | 18568.580702035 | OPTIMAL, same value |

The weight is the linearised moment, Σ d·ln(48/d). Each word's rank mass is fixed by its widths, so at the selected root a* the exact criterion is Σ d·(73/d)^a*. That weight is also LP-optimal at the input (gap below 1e-9). The model relaxes the audit: it omits the hpe cone caps and cold_end conditions and leaves tail frames free. So no frame regroup, coalescence or promotion recipe of any size can raise κ on these words. Lifting every frame to its greatest feasible value costs +3.8%. Annealing over commuting reorders (the `build_gate_moves.py` rule), followed by an exact frame re-solve, gave no gain in 11 restarts (`ORDER-SEARCH.json`). That is a sample, not a proof for all orders.

**Context for κ > 0.01.** Jensen's inequality gives a ≤ −ln p / E_mass[ln(73/r)]. At the current deficit (2560 / 523264), a ≥ 0.01 needs a mass-weighted geometric-mean child rank of at least 44.7; today it is 3.66. At today's child ranks it would instead need a deficit of at least 15,425 (6.0×). Reaching it needs new scalar structure, not frame bookkeeping. About 1,700 of jp8's 2,512 rank-1 climbs are helper unit climbs.

**Files.** `research/frame-lift-search/` contains the model, the LP/CP-SAT solvers, the order search, `RESULT.json` and `ORDER-SEARCH.json`. `tests/test_frame_lift_search.py` checks the lattice model on the in-repo #571 prefix word. There is also a one-line experiment-log link.

**Verification.** `check.py` ran on a fresh `complex-k492-owner-repair/verify.py` rebuild (Linux, Python 3.13) and reports `PASS_FRAME_ONLY_LP_OPTIMAL_FOR_SELECTED_PROVIDERS`. `python3 -m unittest tests.test_frame_lift_search` passes. I did not run `make verify`: no generator, certificate or selected-record file changed.

**Limits.** HiGHS is a floating-point LP, not an exact rational dual certificate, and CP-SAT's `OPTIMAL` comes without a proof log. The scalar program, helper count, dispatch, hosting and bit supplier are out of scope.

prs.body:
The [K492 review](docs/research/community-k492-review.md) leaves one obligation open for #621 (Ali Romman). That PR's `L`-uniform inverse bound still needs paid costs for efficient preparation, rounded execution, restoration and tape. #628 (Chafik Boukhalfa) pays for preparation and neighbouring-stride execution. #764 (Charles Bethin) sharpens the scan rounding. For any stride other than ±1, #628 routes cycles through two merge sorts costing `O(L(B+log L) log L)`. Those sorts bring back the `log L` factor that the inverse bound removed.

This PR adds `research/cyclic-inverse-stride-bridge/` and one CI workflow. **No existing file changes. No new integer κ, complex b, or BIT c.**

## Result

- **Theorem 1.** A Euclidean chain/closure recursion solves `y_i = x_i + b_i y_(i-w)` for any stride. A lag-`w` FIFO built from two stacks gives every pass its predecessor in natural order. Each level at least halves the length. A single stable factor then costs:
  - at most `40L` sequential record moves (largest observed: 29.68 per entry through `L=131072`);
  - `O(L)` rounded operations;
  - an error of at most `min(K,1/β)(u/β)(5+4B/β)+u`.

  The error bound holds for every `L`. The proof reuses #764's shared-suffix identity `1-Q ≥ βG`. A concavity argument shows that coefficient margins never fall below `β` at any recursion depth.
- **Theorem 2.** Composing the solver with #628's certified factorization gives `P(τZ_L^w)^{-1}` at precision `p+(n+2)g+O(log r) = p+O(r^4)`, with no `L` term. One admission condition, `p ≥ log2(log2 L+2)`, depends on `L`.
- **Verdict.** For one kernel inverse on fixed sequential tapes, the cost with all four obligations paid is `soft-O(r^3(p+r^4)) + O(rL)·M(p+r^4) + O(rL(p+r^4))`. That cost per entry does not depend on `L`, so **#621's gain survives payment at the single-kernel level**. Restoration in this model is cheap: the input tape is never written, and scratch tapes are erased at linear cost.

## Validation

`python3 -B -I -O research/cyclic-inverse-stride-bridge/verify.py --check` prints `PASS_CYCLIC_INVERSE_STRIDE_BRIDGE generic=2052 kernel_cases=300 controls=4 max_records_per_entry=29.671875`. It passed under system Python and the repository venv (Python 3.13, Linux). It needs only the standard library and takes about 100 seconds.

- **Generic cases (2052).** `L=1..18`, every stride in `[-L,L)`, three margins and two grids. Each case is compared exactly with an independent per-cycle geometric-closure oracle. The margin invariant is checked at every recursion level.
- **Kernel cases (300).** These use all ten #628 certified kernels (radix 3 through 16), two gauges, `L ∈ {1,2,3,5,8}` and all strides for `L≤5`. Each case checks Theorem 2's exact budget together with #628's perturbation bound and the expanded residual. 81 cases are also compared with a dense Gauss–Jordan solve.
- **Controls.** The replay rejects a rotated closure reseed, too little precision, a unit coefficient and a wrong inner-shift direction.
- **Vendored sources.** The #628 files are byte-identical to head `0768f97d` and are hash-pinned; the verifier refuses drift.
- **Repository checks (Linux, base `66849e1`).** I did not complete a full `make verify`.
  - `make verify` passed seven targets with no failures: `verify-community`, `verify-producers`, `verify-partial-gauge`, `verify-three-stage-cover`, `verify-paired-cube`, `verify-recycled-bit` and `verify-entrance-banks`. My one-hour local limit then stopped the run during `gen4-bank-verify`.
  - `make selected-record-check` and `make verify-tests` passed separately: 549 tests, 0 failures, exit 0.
  - I did not run `frontier626-verify` or the later targets. This PR changes no existing file and does not affect the selected construction.
  - `git diff --cached --check` passed.

## Still open

- A borrowed-array (dirty) form of the stride solver for the exact-width model. #628's dirty route still covers that model, at `O(p+log(D+1)+r^5)` precision.
- Composition across the complete transform, phase collection and normalization.
- The multiplication reduction.
- The `O(r^4)` guard is a proof bound. Numerical probes put the true `min|P|` near `2^-10` for `r≤32`; those probe values are not certified here.

This is not a formal verification. The written proof carries the all-`L` claims, and the finite cases support the reference implementation.

## Credits

- **#621, Ali Romman (@aliromman).** Kernel and the `L`-uniform bounds.
- **#628, Chafik Boukhalfa (@chafreaky).** Factorization, preparation, phase and dirty-shear budgets, and the vendored certificates.
- **#764, Charles Bethin (@cbethin).** The shared-suffix identity and the inverse-square scan bound.

New work by **Rohan Guliani (@Rohansguliani)**, prepared with substantial AI assistance. Apache-2.0. No literature-priority claim is made.

**No new κ.** This screens the Barnes–Wall lattice BW16 as a unit, using the screen main already applies to the ADE root systems, K12, Leech and the Niemeier lattices (`research/e8-decoder-floors-and-cold14-notes/ade_screen.py`, #620; #598; #606). BW16 has not been screened before. Its ceiling comes out 35% below E8's.

## Change and mathematical scope

One self-contained package, `research/bw16-unit-screen/`, plus one path-filtered workflow and one `.gitattributes` line. No existing file changes.

- **Lattice.** BW16 = RM(1,4) + 2·RM(3,4) + 4ℤ¹⁶ (Construction D). It is rebuilt from code generators. All 4320 minimal vectors are enumerated: the shapes (±2²) and (±1⁸) are proved to be the only norm-8 vectors. They give 2160 lines.
  - Every line has the same \|⟨x, y⟩\| profile: {0: 855, 2: 1024, 4: 280}.
- **Window.**
  - `data/clique72.json` holds 72 pairwise non-orthogonal lines. A deterministic greedy reproduces it exactly.
  - At the decoder pattern of `format-limits` §C.6 (#446 Theorem A), the clique forces B[K, K] = I, so the window is c ≥ 72. For comparison, E8 has c = 9, and its largest non-orthogonal set is exactly 8, which is also checked.
  - The pattern's natural decoder B₀ has F₂ rank 191, so 72 ≤ c_min ≤ 191.
- **Screen.**
  - The screen uses `ade_screen.py`'s proxy x = c·h/v = 8/15 and #595's certified `skel.X`, imported unchanged.
  - Result: X(s, 16, 1, 8/15) ≤ 3.8923·10⁻³ at every s = 3…39. That is 0.649× E8's bit ceiling (6.0005·10⁻³, reproduced) and below the full-E8 ceiling (5.1598·10⁻³).
- **Break-even.** BW16 loses at every s if and only if c ≥ 63. So the conclusion does not depend on finding the largest clique.
- **Cause of the loss.** It is entirely the copy charge. With free copies, X(3, 16, 1, 0) = 1.96·10⁻², more than 3× E8's ceiling.

**Scope.**
- This is a ranking screen of the same kind as main's ADE, Leech and Niemeier screens. It is not a κ bound.
- Only decoders on the §C.6 pattern are covered. k = 1, and helper cost is not priced (#620 §4). BW16 has 855 orthogonal neighbours per line against E8's 63, which points the same way.

**Duplicates.** Checked against main at `f567884a` and against the titles and bodies of every hub PR through #883: none screens BW16. The Gaussian E8 clique ceilings (#738, #770, #868) concern a different unit.

## Validation

`python3 -B research/bw16-unit-screen/bw16_check.py` uses the standard library only. It prints `PASS_BW16_UNIT_SCREEN (21 checks)` in about 2 min 40 s. It passed on Linux aarch64 with Python 3.12.3 and 3.11.16, against main at `f567884a`. CI runs it on Python 3.11 and 3.14.

- Joel Pulikkan (GamingPuzzled): #620's unit screen.
- The authors of #446, #598 and #606.
- BW16 and Construction D are classical (Barnes and Wall 1959; Conway and Sloane, *SPLAG*, ch. 4 and 8).

prs.body:
**No new κ.** Main's cover numbers (`research/format-limits` §D, #595) establish that the 63 readers of a bit source (E7 = t⊥) need three hyperplane sections: two flats cover at most 52 lines, and some three D6 flats cover all 63. This package classifies the covers exactly.

## Change and mathematical scope

One self-contained package, `research/e7-flat-cover-classification/`, plus one path-filtered workflow and one `.gitattributes` line. No existing file changes.

1. **The covering triples are exactly the D4 frames through t.**
   - Three hyperplane flats cover E7 if and only if they are E7 ∩ a⊥, E7 ∩ b⊥, E7 ∩ c⊥ for an orthogonal frame {t, a, b, c} spanning a D4.
   - There are 315 such triples, one per D4 through t.
   - The other 3780 orthogonal frames span only 4A1, and their triples miss at least 8 lines.
2. **The near-covers are exactly the A3 subsystems through t.** A near-cover is a triple covering exactly 62 of the 63 lines.
   - Each near-cover is E6(A) + E6(B) + D6(m). Here A and B are the two A2s through t of the A3, and m is the A3's line orthogonal to t, which is the missed line.
   - There are 378 = 63 × 6, and no other type occurs.
3. **The cover count does not force 3 registers per D6 pool.**
   - In a covering triple, each D6 has 16 private lines, which span it.
   - Two rank-5 subflats never cover a whole D6 (at most 28 of 30). But they do cover its 16 private lines (75 pairs per D6), and six rank-5 flats, two per D6, cover all of E7.
   - So "two 5-dim subflats cover ≤ 28 of 30" does not alone give the proposed 180 × 3 = 540 count.

**Consequence for bit skeletons.**
- The D4 skeletons of #493, #510 and #543 read each target through the D6 triple of its 4-frame. By (1), every three-section top layer has this form.
- The only near-alternative is (2), with one line read separately.

**Scope.**
- These are statements about covers by flats, the model of §D. They do not price a skeleton.
- (3) does not construct a 2-per-pool design: frame nesting, the readers' frames and restoration are not modelled.

**Duplicates.**
- Main has the flat census, the best pair and the existence of a D6 cover. It does not classify covers or near-covers.
- #463 has the two-section carrier bound.
- Checked against main at `f567884a` and against the titles and bodies of every hub PR through #883.

## Validation

`python3 -B research/e7-flat-cover-classification/cover_check.py` uses the standard library only.

- **Run.** It prints `PASS_E7_FLAT_COVER_CLASSIFICATION (21 checks)` in about 6 minutes. It passed on Linux aarch64 with Python 3.12.3 and 3.11.16, against main at `f567884a`. CI runs Python 3.11 and 3.14.
- **Exact arithmetic.** Ranks are computed mod 2³¹ − 1. By Hadamard, minors of at most 8 norm-4 rows are at most 256 in absolute value, so these equal the rational ranks.
- **Exhaustive searches.** Every search is exhaustive.
- **Agreement with main.** The checker confirms main's pinned D1 values (8821 flats, the size histogram, the best pair 52, cover number 3) both from its own census and from the text of `d1_cover_numbers.py`.

## Credits and AI disclosure

- DreamingOfClouds: #595's cover-number census and #463's carrier bound.
- eumemic: the D4 skeleton of #493 and #543.
- Prepared by DaysSky with assistance from Claude.

PR846's arbitrary-stride cyclic inverse has a precision admission depending on `log log L`. This removes that condition and combines the unchanged solver with PR862's common-operator bound to give **working precision `W <= p+m+9r^3` at every cycle length and stride**, under the inherited certified prime-power preparation hypotheses. **No new kappa.**

For margin `beta=2^-g` and working precision `W>=2g+8`, rounded chain coefficients vanish after at most `2g+ceil(log2 W)+4` effective levels. A zero-coefficient subtree in the original solver returns exactly the once-rounded data. An explicit early-exit version therefore has identical output, letting the accuracy proof use the bounded effective depth while the unchanged implementation retains its original **40L** record-traffic bound. The optional early-exit version costs at most **44L**, including the coefficient scan and head return.

Its local error fits PR862's existing partial-inverse argument. The package supplies exact cubic budgets for execution, root preparation and integer guards; the supplied-phase cost is `soft-O(r^3(p+m+r^3)) + O(rL) M(A+B_tau) + O(rL(A+B_tau))`, with `A=max(p,w)+2m+16r^3`. Phase-oracle/input costs remain explicit. The Python reference does not claim to implement the inherited fast factorizer or asymptotically fast integer arithmetic.

Validation on the frozen package:

- Complete macOS/Python 3.11 and Linux/Python 3.14 replays with identical full mathematical receipts, under isolation and optimization.
- 423 array cases, 90 coefficient-decay paths, all 300 original PR846 kernel cases and 64 actual cubic-budget kernel executions. The latter round prepared roots to the stated width, verify every common-operator hypothesis and meet the 128-bit target with arbitrary odd lowest working bits.
- 216 exact budget rows, three nonnegative polynomial identities, 54 admission checks, 1,545 logarithm boundaries, 12 new mathematical controls and four inherited controls. Traffic checks cover lengths through 131,072.
- Eleven package rejection controls and a complete read-only relocated replay on each platform. Linux also runs the supplied source package read-only under a supervisor with exit status zero.
- All 12 retained source files match their pinned SHA256 and Git objects. Selected-record consistency passes on current base `bbc600db2fc15007b7c914f4f2b2ed55fa909c87`; staged whitespace and file-byte checks pass.

Reproduce with `python3 -I -O -B research/cyclic-stride-effective-depth/verify.py` and `python3 -I -O -B research/cyclic-stride-effective-depth/test_package.py`. Scoped Python 3.11/3.14 CI is included; hosted results are separate from local validation.

Only the construction/validation directories and their workflow are added. This remains PR846's **clean scratch tape model**, separate from PR951's neighboring-cycle dirty-array work. It does not provide bit-reversible arithmetic, common labels, full transform composition or the multiplication reduction. Finite checks and the written all-size argument are distinct; no independent human review or formal verification is claimed.

## Result

Implement the borrowed-array form left open by [PR #846](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/846) for constant stable coefficients and supplied unit gauges. This research construction adds an arbitrary-stride cyclic inverse to a dirty target, restores the source exactly, and uses no extra data array inside a leaf. It uses a constant number of clean arithmetic registers plus an index stack. The certified [PR #628](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/628) kernels use their original `ceil(log2(r-1))` borrowed arrays, routed over two physical tapes.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/da1cdf8ed4ac9b1b8378dfec73f77ff4e81a4f70/research/dirty-stride-source-reuse/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/da1cdf8ed4ac9b1b8378dfec73f77ff4e81a4f70/research/dirty-stride-source-reuse/VALIDATION.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/da1cdf8ed4ac9b1b8378dfec73f77ff4e81a4f70/research/dirty-stride-source-reuse/SOURCE.json).

Source-prefix closure reuse and reversible block transport give `O(L)` rounded scalar operations and `O(L)` data-record movement per leaf. [PROOF.md](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/da1cdf8ed4ac9b1b8378dfec73f77ff4e81a4f70/research/dirty-stride-source-reuse/PROOF.md) includes rounding, scalar coefficient preparation, complete recursion, temporary magnitude, and tape costs. The reference uses exact rational arithmetic with explicit rounding; it is not a fast-bit compiler or a runtime speedup claim. The precision budget is conservative and does not import the stronger bounds in [PR #877](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/877) or [PR #905](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/905).

The rounded increment can depend on the initial target. A length-three witness and a deliberately wrong inverse order check this distinction. Negative calls reverse the complete word.

## Reproduce

With standard-library Python 3.11 or later:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/dirty-stride-source-reuse/verify.py

The source data, targets, and borrowed arrays have odd lowest working bits.

prs.body:
PR621 bounds every cyclotomic embedding by the same worst-case coefficient height. Averaging those heights before applying the algebraic norm improves the uniform circle-separation exponent from O(r³) to O(r² log² r). The proof covers every prime-power radix and every primitive embedding. No new kappa is claimed.

For `ell = ceil(log2 r)`, `n = r-1`, and `D = phi(r)`, the explicit bound is

```text
|P(z)| >= 2^-d on |z| = 1,
d = 1 + 2ell + n D min(r, 8ell²).
```

The minimum preserves the previous bound at small radices. At r=4096, the sufficient circle exponent drops from 34,351,349,785 to 9,661,317,145. These are analytic bound values, not executed word sizes.

The derivation bounds the discrete Fourier mass of `log|1-zeta^s|`, averages geometric sums over primitive residues, and uses the resulting total height in PR621's resultant/cofactor proof. It neither assumes that the resultant is rational nor treats an average height as a pointwise bound; exact counterexamples reject both shortcuts.

Substituting the new circle exponent into the retained PR862/977 estimates gives, for `N=r² ell²`, fractional working precision `W<=p+m+60N`, integer guard `G<=m+26N`, and preparation precision `b<=p+m+34N`. The inherited clean-scratch arbitrary-stride record count is unchanged. No new inverse execution, dirty-array construction, common-label compiler, complete transform or multiplication reduction is supplied.

Validation includes 17 outward-rounded rational interval cases, six resultants checked independently with SymPy and PR621's rational field arithmetic, and 752 exact integer budgets. Complete macOS/Python 3.11 and Linux/Python 3.14 replays produce byte-identical receipts. Both platforms also reject eleven package faults and replay from a read-only relocated copy. The Linux job terminated successfully under supervision. Twelve retained source files have verified Git-object and SHA256 pins. The selected-record check and all 25 related tests pass at base `2921874911956718fcaaaf9396fe8267b3cfa9f0`.

Reproduce with the pinned dependency installed:

```sh
python -m pip install -r research/averaged-cyclotomic-height/requirements.txt
python -I -O -B research/averaged-cyclotomic-height/verify.py
python -I -O -B research/averaged-cyclotomic-height/test_package.py
```

Credit Ali Romman's #621, the retained OpenAI/classical kernel lineage, and #628, #862 and #977; the latter retains Rohan Guliani's #846 and Charles Bethin's #764. Original proofs and notices are included. This work has substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human review, formal verification, practical speedup or literature-priority claim is made. The full repository suite and selected cold replay were not run for this isolated package. Main still selects #942 at `1661960547713947/10^18`.
