Extend [PR #985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/985) from constant site coefficients to the nonconstant quadratic
diagonal `D_j=exp(2 pi i a j^2/m)`. The leaf adds an approximation to
`(I-b D Z^w D^-1)^-1 x` to an arbitrary dirty target and restores the source
exactly. Its negative call reverses the complete grid word. The complete
factor interface keeps the original logarithmic borrowed-array count,
restores every borrowed array, and pays four phase passes around the whole
word. No phase array, cache, or free phase lookup is used.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/99c71d385171480ecc2c43287aa4a04e1027fcd9/research/dirty-stride-phases/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/99c71d385171480ecc2c43287aa4a04e1027fcd9/research/dirty-stride-phases/VALIDATION.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/99c71d385171480ecc2c43287aa4a04e1027fcd9/research/dirty-stride-phases/SOURCE.json).

`exp(-pi i s j^2/t)` for even `L=t`. For `L=8,a=-3,m=16,w=3`, the edge phases
have residues `11,9,7,5,3,1,15,13`; the ideal response differs from the
unphased response by more than `1/8` in a real component.

The implementation uses exact finite differences, a rounded Machin/Taylor
evaluator, three reversible real shears, and exact quarter-turns. The proof
bounds coefficient error and both directions of rounded conjugation,
including large dirty targets. Phase preparation costs `O((L+1)P)` scalar
steps with `P=W+O(log W)`. The full bill includes descriptors, input and
scratch storage, scalar widths, recurrence counters, data access, and tape
returns. This is a slower paid phase interface, with no fast-bit or runtime
speedup claim.

prs.title: Finite BIT construction: R438 source boundary with full hosted invoice

prs.body:
## What this is

**Research note + independent verification. No κ claim; the bit side does not bind.**

It prices a bit word from its **paid profile alone**, and then uses that to run an exhaustive audit of
the merged bit supplier (PR #589's tuned R439 word). Everything is exact integer/rational arithmetic
against files pinned by sha256 at `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`.

New material:

1. **The paid-profile duality.** The certified saving `c` of a bit word is the unique `a > 0` with
   `Psi(a) := sum_r n_r r((m/r)^a - 1) = D := m*W - rank_mass`. Equivalently, for any fixed `a0`,
   `c` is a strictly decreasing function of the single weighted count `G(a0) = sum_r n_r r^(1-a0)`.
   Rank-profile search is therefore a *linear-objective* problem and a candidate word costs `O(#gates)`
   to price with no root finding.
   Verified by re-deriving `c` from the profile with an independent rational `ln`/`exp` interval
   implementation (`code/bitprof.py`): the lower endpoint of the resulting `10^-24` bracket is
   **exactly** the shipped value for both #555 and #589
   (`1733427039589844234749/10^24`). The shipped values include the pipeline's inherited bad-envelope
   surcharge (`32 m^2 (sum n) m^a / 10^16`), which moves the root by `2.01e-12` — two units on the
   24-digit grid, so it cannot be dropped; the verifier checks both roots.

2. **The objective decomposes over registers**, so a `k`-move improvement requires the `k` moves to
   share registers. That is what makes a complete two-move search affordable.

3. **The audit.** On the merged #589 word, priced on the exact objective:

   | check | result |
   |---|---|
   | nominated single moves | 9,347 |
   | strictly improving single moves | **0** |
   | cost-neutral plateau | 9,263 |
   | improving Steinberg 3→2 moves (671 triples) | **0** |
   | legal `(slot, frame)` pairs over 3,064 operations | 9,933 |
   | operations whose nominated frame is not exact-objective optimal | **0** |
   | complete register-adjacent two-move neighbourhood (`--full`) | 645,900 pairs |
   | best two-move delta | **0**, exactly |

   **Positive control:** steepest descent on the exact objective from PR #555's base word applies
   exactly two moves — PR #589's hoist (`A[2034] → slot 2028, frame 79`) and sink
   (`A[2041] → slot 2076, frame 517`) — and lands on the tuned word's profile and objective. The
   machinery rederives #589 rather than being told about it.

## What it is worth

It closes the reframing avenue for the merged bit supplier at one and two moves: any further bit
saving from this word has to come from a mechanism outside the class (geometry, decoder constant,
helper count, hosting), not from moving gates. It also gives the exact marginal exchange rate
(`dc/c = -(dG/G)/(a(ln m - E[ln r]))`) so a future move can be priced before it is built, and it
independently corroborates the fixed point that PR #589's tuner claims, on a different objective
implementation.

## Concurrent work (refreshed 2026-10-13)

Rebased onto `main` @ `29218749`; every pinned input is byte-identical on both commits, and both
`make bit-profile-pair-audit-verify` and the unittest module were re-run on the rebased tree.

These landed while this note was being prepared, and they are **consistent with** rather than
counterexamples to the fixed point above:

* **#1043** improves the *same* #589 word by a mechanism outside the reframing class — deleting
  `helper470` via a caller-boundary read of `source77`, giving R438 and
  `c = 0.001734176288479865766692`. That is a helper/register rewrite, exactly the "outside the class"
  route the audit points at.
* **#1040 / #1047** cut complete ADD counts on a different R439 lineage (post-PR915/PR967), and
  **#1045** crosses PR941's disjoint-pair floor with a four-helper fusion. Different words, different
  accounting, different move classes.
* Those results are cited from their own packages and were **not** re-run here.

## Scope and limits

* Finite, exact audit of two specific words and one move class. Not an optimality theorem over bit
  words, and **not** an exclusion of three-or-more-move escapes of the plateau.
* The two-move search is complete for the nominated move set; the nomination's completeness at the
  frame level is separately certified (0 of 3,064 operations disagree).
* The tuner's proxy objective is *not* identical to the exact objective (largest absolute discrepancy
  `1.645e-5` on this word); only its argmin agrees, which is why everything here is priced exactly.
* No κ change; bit headroom only. Nine-stage price only.
* Every interface that #543, #555 and #589 retain remains assumed. This is not a Lean proof of
  integer multiplication.

## Reproduce

```sh
make bit-profile-pair-audit-verify        # ~6 min, all checks except the pair search
make bit-profile-pair-audit-full-verify   # ~35 min, adds the complete two-move neighbourhood
```

No C++ toolchain, Boost, Lean or network access; only Python 3.11+, `numpy` (for the pinned tuner) and
the pinned files on main.

## Files

`research/bit-profile-pair-audit/` (README, `verify.py`, `EXPECTED.json`, `code/`), plus

prs.body:
[PR #985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/985) uses a length admission and a conservative fifth-degree sufficient precision bound for its target-dependent rounded dirty word. This contribution proves an all-length admission and a cubic sufficient precision bound for that same constant-coefficient word. It retains the full recursion, exact source and scratch restoration, two physical data tapes, and all movement costs.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6bc675be1554b3a3be771147f21f9dc2c6dae50a/research/dirty-stride-precision/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6bc675be1554b3a3be771147f21f9dc2c6dae50a/research/dirty-stride-precision/VALIDATION.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6bc675be1554b3a3be771147f21f9dc2c6dae50a/research/dirty-stride-precision/SOURCES.json).

For a certified prime-power radix `r`, initial norm at most `2^m`, target error `2^-p`, and incoming grid width `w_input`, the sufficient fractional width is at most `max(p,w_input)+m+18r^3`. The signed integer reserve is at most `m+15r^3`. The proof bounds inverse errors at the positive preimage and pays for that preimage in the integer guard. It proves a zero-subtree identity and a depth-independent internal magnitude bound for the actual dirty word; it does not assume the clean-scratch [PR #977](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/977) identity transfers.

The common-operator subset and prefix estimates are credited to [PR #862](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/862) and [PR #905](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/905). [PR #985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/985) at [9df42a99dd8497b6e7d46cd2507bb89071372640](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/9df42a99dd8497b6e7d46cd2507bb89071372640) is retained byte-exact, with its full dependency closure. The derived solver changes admission and caches the two validation reads that the simultaneous phase lane ([PR #1038](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1038)) found were read twice but charged once. An independent array observer checks each literal indexed access. Every rounded data operation, recursive child, transport step, and head return is retained.

At `r=64`, `p=128`, and `m=20`, the explicit sufficient fractional budget is 1,420,902 bits; the pinned [PR #985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/985) full-word budget needs 517,236,859 bits with the same margin before any larger structural-depth admission. Both words have 4,000 leaf calls and six borrowed arrays. These are sufficient bounds, not minimum widths or timing gains.

Run:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/dirty-stride-precision/test_package.py
```

The package covers 5,220 budget certificates, 1,088 all-length thresholds, 180 coefficient extinction cases, 8,256 exponent geometries, four dirty zero subtrees, 2,322 retained power cases, 468 signed leaf cases, 80 certified kernel cases, and 18 actual uniform-preparation kernel cases. The 98 kernel cases execute 392 complete signed words and 24,848 leaf calls. A full `L=5741`, stride 2378, 12-bit example is newly admitted and checks its residual, exact inverse, and 3,952,237 paid tape moves. Twelve fault controls and a read-only relocated replay must reproduce the exact receipt. [VALIDATION.json](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6bc675be1554b3a3be771147f21f9dc2c6dae50a/research/dirty-stride-precision/VALIDATION.json) gives the measured local checks and omitted checks.

This is a conditional accuracy theorem with exact-rational supporting checks. The inherited supplied factor-preparation, analytic inverse, and fast scalar arithmetic hypotheses remain. It supplies no all-size factorizer, fast bit compiler, variable site phases, Lean proof, complete transform, new multiplication exponent, or measured end-to-end speedup. The selected certificate and [upstream/](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/6bc675be1554b3a3be771147f21f9dc2c6dae50a/upstream) are unchanged.

Prepared for Ali Romman (@aliromman) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. [NOTICE.md](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6bc675be1554b3a3be771147f21f9dc2c6dae50a/research/dirty-stride-precision/NOTICE.md) preserves predecessor credit and identifies the simultaneous phase-lane accounting finding. No independent human review is claimed.

Concurrent [PR #1025](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1025) at `6ef2168ac90d42926bceb7ac9b2e029463800c76` improves the analytic circle exponent and applies it to [PR #862](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/862), [PR #977](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/977)'s clean-scratch estimates. Its pinned proof explicitly supplies no dirty-array circuit or new inverse execution. This contribution keeps its consumed analytic inputs and proves the [PR #985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/985) dirty-word transfer. A combined tighter dirty budget is a follow-up; [OVERLAP.md](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6bc675be1554b3a3be771147f21f9dc2c6dae50a/research/dirty-stride-precision/OVERLAP.md) records the distinction.

[PR #985](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/985) later advanced to [da1cdf8ed4ac9b1b8378dfec73f77ff4e81a4f70](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/da1cdf8ed4ac9b1b8378dfec73f77ff4e81a4f70) with the same two read-once accounting corrections. This package intentionally retains the exact consumed `9df42a` predecessor. The derived solver includes the corrections and the independent access observer; no moving source was imported.

The frozen standalone package replay returned zero in 740.81 seconds on macOS arm64 with Python 3.14.7 and one CPU. Peak child memory was 41,304,064 bytes. The selected-record check and all 25 selected tests passed. The full repository suite, selected cold replay, and hosted Linux matrix were not run. The local validation record also preserves an earlier successful package run whose external timing wrapper failed after completion because macOS blocked its `sysctl` query.

Later work: Philipp (@mightyOil)'s merged [PR #1295](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1295), at `3a6773708f0d73f7dbee164f4c6e7658b0b41509`, sharpens this conditional sufficient fractional envelope from `max(p,w_input)+m+18r^3` to `max(p,w_input)+m+15r^3`. Its [proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/3a6773708f0d73f7dbee164f4c6e7658b0b41509/research/commuting-dirty-precision/PROOF.md) and [certificate](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/3a6773708f0d73f7dbee164f4c6e7658b0b41509/research/commuting-dirty-precision/CERTIFICATE.json) retain the common immutable commuting operator, leaf contract, inverse-preimage reserve and full operation bill. This is later evidence, not a change to this PR's pinned theorem or validation. The joint dirty-stride proof-interface audit remains open; neither result gives a new kappa.

prs.body:
The cost-63 P111 decoder is known, but its source access, asymmetric COPY
endpoint, exact phase frame and dirty restoration need a physical word. This
PR adds a complete finite complex decoder and an executable coordinate
baseline with the same 674 original streams and physical endpoints. The sole
nonzero COPY endpoint is processed last. All source reads, adapters, copy
lifetimes and three unused rank-nine helper tails are paid.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/d27499553138bde007f5b1163e65e71da1b18899/research/shared-carrier-decoder/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/d27499553138bde007f5b1163e65e71da1b18899/research/shared-carrier-decoder/EXPECTED.json) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/d27499553138bde007f5b1163e65e71da1b18899/research/shared-carrier-decoder/SOURCES.json).

The complete recursive profile changes from
`896 H1 + 444 H7 + 238 H8` to
`945 H1 + 497 H7 + 182 H8 + 3 H9`. An exact uniform inequality proves a smaller
recursive moment for `0 <= b <= 1/256`, including the selected complex
exponent at the pinned base. **The candidate also costs 108 more AXPY scans,
126 more dyadic scalar multiplications per address, and 392 more adapter
scans.** This is a construction and a recursive-cost comparison; it is not a
runtime gain, selected-supplier improvement, or new kappa.

The proof binds each logical event to its exact live Clifford frame. It proves
the complete physical map and its inverse transpose, including allocation and
disposal of the one temporary stream. Dirty helpers recover their logical
inputs at FULL, so their physical outputs are F times their initial arrays.
They are not claimed to have physical identity endpoints.

Validation uses exact rational replay of all 674 independent logical columns,
a separate integer-column interpreter, every native phase and child rank,
four whole physical executions on 512 complex addresses per role, and every
matrix column of the rank-seven COPY. Eleven broken-word controls address
compensation, cleanup, source access, endpoint order, helper tails, temporary
lifetime, phase and recursive charge. Three further controls reject a missing
receipt and Boolean or float substitutions for integer receipt fields. Normal
and optimized relocated replays passed, as did a changed-source rejection and
the selected-record check. The coordinator separately replayed a second dense
input in both candidate orientations. Reproduction is:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/shared-carrier-decoder/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/shared-carrier-decoder/test_controls.py
```

The exact Gaussian physical replay is finite. A written composition proof
supplies its all-input conclusion. The package gives a conservative quadratic
finite tape-route bound; it does not claim the all-size linear tape, rounding,
side-correction, external endpoint, host-owner or outer-assembly obligations.

The new work is confined to [research/shared-carrier-decoder/](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/tree/d27499553138bde007f5b1163e65e71da1b18899/research/shared-carrier-decoder) at base
[8bddbee377e2f3ce1f1247196c4b290d55767d20](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/8bddbee377e2f3ce1f1247196c4b290d55767d20). Selected and upstream files stay
unchanged. [PR #717](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/717) and [PR #968](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/968) receive credit for the complex decoder and the
copy-cost result; [PR #620](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/620), [PR #757](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/757), [PR #761](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/761) receive related depth-one credit. [PR #998](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/998),
[PR #1008](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1008) and [PR #1020](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1020) concern different structural classes and do not supply this
physical construction. The exact compiler is retained and pinned from
@icekylinx's [PR #531](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/531) lineage. Prepared for Ali Romman (@aliromman) with substantial
OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. No independent human review is claimed.

prs.body:
This adds a source-bound Lean proof of the scalar cleanup-prefix rewrite used by the CK `hyperplane_end` constructor. It proves that moving selected gates to the front in recipe order preserves the scalar program, including arbitrary input states, disjoint self-adds, and unsorted selections.

The concrete instance checks all 2,869 original instructions, 34 selected cleanup gates, and 19,084 original-prefix commutation pairs. Its original selection certificate (#626 at `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`) is retained byte-for-byte, so advancing the repository selection does not invalidate this historical audit. All actual constructor, recipe, and inventory inputs remain hash-pinned. Changes are confined to `research/cleanup-prefix-lean/`.

Validation:
- A separate Codex reviewer reproduced a clean Lean 4.27.0 build and audited the axioms; no `sorry`, `native_decide`, or additional axioms were found.
- Independent exact arithmetic checks cover all 716 source input columns, reproduce the original constructor output, and reject corrupted artifacts and weakened-rule counterexamples.
- Generator checks compare every instruction and coefficient against the source-bound fixture. Targeted runner tests reject prerelease and other non-exact Lean versions.
- Frozen-certificate portability controls require later or absent live selection metadata to leave the audit unchanged and corrupted frozen metadata to fail; independent publication review accepted with no remaining findings.
- Isolated clean application and source/generator replay passed against both the original base and upstream `abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf`; final patch application and all 28 resulting files were checked again after documentation finalization.

Scope and trust: this proves a scalar reordering theorem with associative/commutative addition and arbitrary multiplication, with an `Int` instance supplied. Python source/JSON binding and generation remain an explicit trusted bridge. Rational/complex interpretations, the complete multiplication theorem, frame/accounting and all-size/analytic-transfer obligations are outside this contribution. No new κ or frontier change is claimed.

This builds on the commuting-prefix constructors in #601/#608, HPE formal interfaces in #593/#599, and the #622/#623/#626 construction lineage. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance was used for implementation and separate-agent review; no human review is claimed. See README.md, REVIEW.md, FINAL-REVIEW.json and ACCEPTANCE.json in the package for reproducible commands, exact pins, evidence, limitations and finding resolutions.

The PR combines Jeremy Kothe's unchanged #1022 seven-slot k8 supplier with a new 333-call order and an exact integer-flow construction of 159,840 whole-helper owners. The constructor expands the frozen flow through deterministic bipartite matching, without an owner optimizer. The idle profile is `{1:5622,48:11302}`; the independent owner checker and emitted-controller invoice agree. The charged prefix reserve is 1,024 bits (actual 775), and the row coefficient is 17,495 < 20,161.

[PR #1038](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1038) evaluates Machin and Taylor series at every data site. This package
replaces that phase interface with two reversible dyadic phase states.
It uses a fixed second difference, bounded three-shear rotations, and
`Q=W+2 bit_length(L+1)+20` state bits. Every pass reconstructs its phase
state backward. Seed and chart coefficients clear exactly. No phase
array or checkpoint list is stored.

Review files: [Proof and scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1627bf208f80e490522343590dd52f38b329e238/research/dirty-stride-fast-phases/PROOF.md) · [Evidence](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1627bf208f80e490522343590dd52f38b329e238/research/dirty-stride-fast-phases/VALIDATION.md) · [Source pins and credit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1627bf208f80e490522343590dd52f38b329e238/research/dirty-stride-fast-phases/SOURCE.json).

The proof gives a uniform quadratic drift bound and the same emitted
coefficient accuracy as [PR #1038](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1038). The retained dirty wrappers therefore
keep their large-target error bound, exact source and borrowed-array
restoration, original precision, and two-data-tape movement bill. One
prepared phase object serves all four passes of a complete dirty word.
Its stream uses `60L+6` real products and `24L` chart divisions. Exact
seed preparation and erasure add `O(P)` scalar operations on wider
rational operands, where `P=Q+24`.

Status: enabling construction. The elementary phase bit bound is
`O((A+V)^2+P S^2+L T^2)`, where `A` is the original numerator width,
`V` is the modulus width, `S=16(P+V+1)^2`, and `T` covers stream and
data widths. A direct reversible arithmetic compiler needs
`O((A+V)^2+S^2+T^2)` clean scratch bits. The Python reference implements
the scalar state and exact series cleanup; it does not emit a native
bit-gate program. No new kappa is claimed.

The base is [abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/abdc6a7002abdbcd9e21bfc5e1a795784deacfdf). [PR #1038](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1038) is pinned
at [99c71d385171480ecc2c43287aa4a04e1027fcd9](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/99c71d385171480ecc2c43287aa4a04e1027fcd9); nine retained files have
Git-blob and SHA256 pins. No moving selected-result file is source-pinned.
[PR #1054](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1054) and [PR #1025](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1025) are scope references, not combined theorems. The
inherited logarithmic borrowed-array pool stays fixed. Supplier hosting,
factor production, multi-axis composition, and outer assembly stay open.

Verification:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/dirty-stride-fast-phases/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/dirty-stride-fast-phases/test_package.py
```

The main receipt covers 98 phase cases, 1,474 rational interval samples,
16 dirty words, three same-input work comparisons, and seven input or
lifecycle controls. It executes and reverses all 16,384 steps of the
long case. The package check rejects seven semantic faults and source
corruption, then replays the full receipt from read-only relocated files.
It returned 0 in 245.149 seconds. The parent agent also completed the
optimized main replay. These checks are finite evidence for the written
proof, not independent human review or formal multiplication verification.

Timing results are mixed. Three alternating same-input trials give
[PR #1038](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1038)/new median seconds of `0.042217/0.191425` at `(L,W)=(32,16)`,
`0.689942/1.286691` at `(257,48)`, and `10.187936/9.092779` at
`(2048,96)`. New seed erasure is included. Seed operands reach 55,767
bits in the last case. All final trials and an earlier run's medians
are disclosed. The shared-host timings do not establish a general
speedup. The result is the proved interface and its separate work bill.

[NOTICE.md](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1627bf208f80e490522343590dd52f38b329e238/research/dirty-stride-fast-phases/NOTICE.md) preserves predecessor credit and discloses substantial OpenAI
Codex assistance. New material is by Ali Romman (@aliromman) under Apache-2.0.

## Change and mathematical scope

This proposes the conditional finite witness **κ = 0.001675560947524449**. An exact within-call permutation therefore transfers the preceding T16 packing without another owner search.

The final local word uses demoted entrance groups **603, 611, and 635**, with local profile `{1:2364,2:498,3:412,4:130,5:82,8:8}`. **Start review at `research/k8-joint-entrances/README.md`, `PROOF.md`, `CLAIM.json`, and `verify.py`.** The branch also includes its four additive predecessor packages: `k8-coordinated-owners`, `k8-eight-ends`, `k8-eight-ends-t16`, and `k8-three-demotions`. The new exact fixed-word, fixed-inventory all-replica grid upper bound is **0.001675568675201533**. It is an upper relaxation, not an achieved construction or a bound on other circuits, mixed suppliers, or recursion geometries.

The unchanged PR589 bit supplier, PR559 recurrence correction, and bit bad-residue surcharge remain. All-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, precision/tape, analytic-transfer, and bit H1–H5 assumptions remain. This is not an unconditional multiplication theorem or full Lean certification. The selected repository certificate is unchanged.

## Validation

The final package passed:

- Fresh native exact forward and dual replay of all **704 columns**, with **2,904 directed phase checks**.
- **27 new local semantic controls**.
- Unchanged admission engines: **69 assembly, 12 bit-supplier, 15 controller, and six independent T16 negative controls**; **47 strict outer inequalities**.

- Two exact arithmetic engines for the fixed-family ceiling, with independent enumeration of all **1,163 bin patterns**.
- Source and manifest bindings, Python compilation, and whitespace checks. All **82 pinned source files shared with upstream main at `ce7ad1b6`** are unchanged; the remaining pinned files are predecessor packages added on this branch.

Fresh reproduction (Python 3.11+, C++ compiler, Boost; choose a new output directory outside the repository):

```sh
CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH=/path/to/boost python -B research/k8-joint-entrances/verify.py \
  --base "$BASE" --work /absolute/new/output-directory
```

`BASE` is the original R480 k8 + seven-slot word pinned in `research/k8-eight-ends/RECIPE.json`. No optimization solver runs during verification. Reproduction details and explicit replay-reuse options are in the README.

All **18 repository `make verify` groups completed across the initial and resumed runs**, including all **87 isolated test modules** and **20 patch applicability checks**. This was not one successful `make verify` invocation: the initial system-Python attempt stopped on missing `int.bit_count`, and the Python 3.11 run later stopped because Apple clang rejects `-fopenmp`. The failed and remaining stages then passed under Python 3.11.14 and GCC 16.2.0 (continuation exit 0). No guards, tests, or tracked upstream sources were changed. `evidence/REPOSITORY-VERIFICATION.json` and three archived logs record the complete coverage and both environment failures; this regression result is separate from the package-specific witness admission above.

The search covers all **64 subsets** of six individually selected entrance reductions, followed by **354 same-dimension rotation trials**, a joint fixed-dimension entrance/frame search over **68 helpers**, and a joint dimension-four/five plus aggregate-packing search over **56 helpers**. Another 145 trials removed one-dimensional entrances individually, by point cohort, or all together, again without improvement. Solver output is nomination data, not an exact optimality certificate. A broader formulation over 192 entrances and 1.8 million LP variables returned no solution before its numerical solve limit; it is recorded as inconclusive, not infeasible, and yields no stronger κ.

PR1111 by **seslly/shipstuff**, commit `381831ea554ea983e16224dabed8921b7d0ffdbc`, supplied the **group-635 entrance-demotion lead**. prs.body:
## Result

Conditional **kappa = 0.001673260706543984**, compared with the frozen [PR1117](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1117) claim **0.001672846995880185** at `342b67f23dfa8f41a520a0d58978b2875e9eb0dd`.

The absolute gain is **0.000000413710663799**, approximately **0.02473093 percent** relative. This is a concrete combined kernel-and-owner improvement under the inherited conditional interfaces. It is not an unconditional multiplication theorem or a claim that the full open-proposal queue has been accepted.

Only `research/adaptive-kernel-demotion/` is added. The selected certificate, upstream sources and existing submissions are unchanged.

## Mechanism: choose the kernel prefix to fit the actual pending stock

PR1117 supplies the rank-seven end word and its T16 owner schedule. PR1111 supplies a four-helper entrance-demotion recipe. Applying one fixed provider everywhere ignores the actual pending capacities. This package constructs and checks five joint local prefixes and chooses the prefix separately at every literal call:

1. Groups are ordered **635, 603, 611, 619, 627**. Their helper indices are respectively `(411,413,414,415)`, `(379,381,382,383)`, `(387,389,390,391)`, `(395,397,398,399)`, and `(403,405,406,407)`.
2. Prefix `k` changes exactly `4k` helper widths from four to five. The complete local profile change is `k * (-8H1 + 8H2 + 4H3 - 4H4)`, verified by recounting each actual joint word, rather than assuming recipe gains add.
3. Within a call, selected helper occurrences eligible to use their own slack remain in place. The remaining selected occurrences exchange owners bijectively with distinct width-four donor occurrences. Every extra width consumes an actual unused axis; all shared owner remainders are updated before the next insertion.
4. Every insertion uses a gap pattern `[1,1,1,r]`, with `r` equal to one, two or three. The resulting complete local-plus-remainder differences are respectively `-12H1+8H2+4H3-4H4`, `-10H1+7H2+4H3-4H4`, and `-11H1+9H2+3H3-4H4`. The written proof establishes strict moment improvement for every `0 < b < 1`.
5. Before these insertions, one legal three-owner cycle replaces two rank-six remainders by rank one and rank eleven: `+H1 - 2H6 + H11`. This preserves all literal helper occurrences and has a strict concavity saving for every `0 < b < 1`.

The realized assignment contains **359 group demotions across 103 of 144 calls**: 356 four-unit patterns, one `[1,1,1,2]` pattern and two `[1,1,1,3]` patterns. Prefixes zero through five occur **41, 24, 8, 15, 6 and 50 times**. These counts come from the final table and dispatch; no advertised kappa gains are added together.

## Complete paid profile and exact pricing

```text
{1:344363, 2:65097, 3:62855, 4:19012, 5:11808,
 7:8, 8:1152, 11:2, 48:4873}
```

Live stock remains **14,336**, paid rank mass **1,041,408**, and deficit **5,120**. The final map has **6,034 paid idle remainders**, 1,433 fewer than PR1117, and **9,898 actual 73-column chart types**, compared with 10,057. The complete literal difference contains **4,594 owner records**; unchanged rows are retained exactly.

Both retained exact rational moment engines certify the native and conservative endpoints. The complete outer assembly checks **all 47 strict inequalities**. The bit supplier remains the pinned inherited supplier; the complex side binds. Finite work, adapters, restoration and the six-provider dispatch are retained in the invoice instead of being treated as free.

## Reproduction and checked scope

Python 3.10+ and its standard library, from the repository root, using a fresh output directory outside this package:

```sh
python -I -B research/adaptive-kernel-demotion/verify.py --out ../adaptive-result
```

The delivered verifier binds the complete source inventory and checks:

- Every actual joint prefix on all **704 arbitrary input columns**, including dirty helpers, in forward and inverse-transpose orientations; native emitted words and **25 corruption controls per provider**.
- The changed phase edges and wrappers for each prefix. These are fresh checks of the changed local constructions, not a cold reconstruction of every unchanged ancestral phase.
- Every one of the **69,120 literal roles**, all 144 calls, their actual provider widths, independent source-derived inactivity windows, physical family uniqueness, chronological coordinate blocks and actual orthogonal 73-column charts.
- A complete remainder/profile recount, all nine finite invoice guards, exact native/conservative and inherited-bit moment brackets, and all 47 strict outer inequalities. Negative controls and source/manifest binding remain explicit.

The changed local constructions, adaptive dispatch and new owner map are concretely checked. The all-size/compiler, common-label and mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting interface, precision/tape and exact-recovery, analytic-transfer and inherited bit-contract assumptions remain conditional. No complete ancestral cold replay, new Lean certificate, hosted CI pass, independent human review or global packing optimum is claimed.

## Mathematical sources and future reuse

The package notes and source ledger in `research/adaptive-kernel-demotion/README.md` record two distinct OpenAI-proof mechanisms investigated by each of the four workers, including their exact source statements and their actual contribution or limitation. In the owner construction, alternating matching-layer switches provide the cycle replacement, and a disjoint first-hit projector partition supplies the canonical self-donor/external-donor separation. The other worker ledgers explain the local transfer, inventory, dispatch and arithmetic adaptations.

These are explicitly sourced adaptations. They are not eight independently additive exponent improvements or new priority claims for the underlying mathematics. The reusable contribution is the checked sufficient coupling: actual joint provider prefixes plus literal donor assignments and a uniform saving proof. The notes retain the one-group fallback, bounded allocation comparisons and routes that were not assigned numerical gains.

## Credit and disclosure

Direct construction inputs: **PR1117** (rank-seven ends and frozen T16 owners), **PR1111** (entrance demotion), and **PR1030** (the demotion/lowering context). Local and schedule ancestry: **PR1018/987** (seven slots), **PR1005/1004** (mutable-leaver cells), **PR1022/858** (T16 and whole-family owner scheduling), together with **PR869, PR799, PR741, PR685 and PR645**. **PR635** and its retained notices record the ported cold-end, frame, native compiler and source lineage; **PR589** supplies the inherited bit endpoint.

**PR1063/1094** provide neutral recolouring and owner-exchange context, and **PR1072** supplies the related promotion-to-gap construction. Their numerical gains are not copied or added to this result. Original author attribution, AI disclosures and the Apache-2.0 license are preserved in the vendored notices.

The new adaptive construction, proofs, independent checks and packaging were prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. No name or email of the submitting user is added by this package, and the assistant did not publish or push anything.

The final self-contained replay passed from the delivered source inventory. It additionally rejects optimized Python and mutated source bytes before running the mathematical checks. The manual browser-upload batch contains 73 files (approximately 7.7 MB), with SHA-256 identity to that inventory.

In Child 15 (capacity $32$), the previous packing left isolated remainder mass at Remainder 5 (Replica 4 Port 86, occupancy $27/32$) and Remainder 6 (Replica 8 Port 111, occupancy $26/32$).

## Summary

Adds `research/exact-frame-toolkit/`: the search and admission tools behind the companion construction PR #1195 (two
source-holder fusions on #1148's joint-entrance k8 word). **No new κ.** No selected record, upstream file or existing package is modified.

**Revision 2 (2026-10-14)** answers the review continuation point
([comment](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1186#issuecomment-6161623948)). It also fixes two harness
screen gaps. Details are in the README sections *What is certified* and *Revision 2*.

**Revision 3 (2026-10-14)** makes the toolkit run on Windows, answering woklerx's independent audit
([comment](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1186#issuecomment-6169503528)). The platform-dependent
pieces move into `compat.py`, `portability.py` checks the Windows code paths on any OS, and the toolkit refuses `-O`.
`frames.py` is unchanged. Results are in `PORTABILITY.json` and the README section *Revision 3*.

- **Frame solver** (`frames.py`). Each solve carries two per-instance certificates:
  - exact optimality for the floored integer surrogate weights `floor(2^40 · lo_r(b))`;
  - with `interval=True`, a rigorous rational interval for the true per-call moment at b over every assignment of the frame
    model.

  The interval's lower end is a chain-dual (or exact-elimination) bound with outward-floored weights on a 2^-224 grid, plus
  a λ·rank shift that telescopes along every register chain. Its upper end is the engines' upper bound of the returned
  assignment. L/U domain propagation, chain dual decomposition and exact elimination; models monotone chains, target caps,
  cut equality, mutable early tails, and `audit_local`'s helper cones as caps (`model.py`).
- **Pricing harness** (`harness.py`): build_tri-style edits (B deletes/inserts, early tails, FULL prepends). Screens, in order:
  1. the auditor's static program rules;
  2. the B+tail+prepend map mod p;
  3. an exact check that the derived compensation is unchanged;
  4. frames.

  Every negative delta and every returned word is re-checked by the unchanged `audit_local.py`. With `interval=True` it also
  returns the true realized delta (`realized_delta_units`) and a bound on any possible true gain (`max_gain_units`).
- **Searches**: read-fusion candidates (`fusion.py`), joint triangle-hybrid candidates (`joint.py`), and the multiprocess
  fusion + enlarged-reader repair sweep (`repair.py --interval`, `sites.py`).
- **Composition**: split a slot recipe and price its instances (`slots.py`); compose slots with fusions (`compose.py`); put a
  newer word's entrances and ends onto a scalar program and re-solve (`transplant.py`).
- **Exact κ** (`kappa.py`): the certified moment root and the retained 47-constraint outer assembly with PR589, for any T.
- **Admission drivers** that reuse unchanged package engines: PR635 native chain (`native.py`), PLAN/SPEC rebinding with
  unchanged widths (`rebind.py`), `unpin.py` between discovery and `freeze_spec.py`, the T16 discovery run
  (`t16_discover.py`), and per-site negative controls (`controls.py`).

Pure Python 3.11+ with NumPy, on Linux, macOS and Windows; no C++, Boost, LP/MILP solver or network. Do not run it with
`-O`: its asserts are checks, so it refuses to start.

## Check

```sh
python -B research/exact-frame-toolkit/selftest.py      # about 50 s here (Python 3.12 and 3.14); --quick about 25 s
python -B research/exact-frame-toolkit/portability.py   # the Windows code paths on any OS, then the selftest
```

On a GitHub Actions Windows runner (Windows Server 2025, Python 3.12.10, NumPy 2.5.4) the full selftest and the portability check pass, `-O` is refused, and the
spawn-mode `repair.py --interval` sweep of the pre-slot word matches the macOS sweep in all 2,405 records
([run](https://github.com/mdumitrean/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38621712253)).

It uses only files on main:
- the retained #1042/#1094 replay archives;
- #1094's `REPLAY.json`;
- #942's checkpoint and the `ASSEMBLY.json` it names.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `kappa.py` on #1094's (T16) and #942's (T37) complex profiles | the selected and checkpoint κ, exactly |
| surrogate frame optimum of the seven-slot k8 word `c2b29430` | its published profile (integer certificate) |
| true-moment interval of that word at b | published frames within 1.48e-11 units of the minimum over the frame model; the surrogate alone bounds this only by 1512 units |
| control: deliberately worse assignment | interval width = its exact true excess (6763.29 units) |
| control: exact dual with multipliers of magnitude 2^62–2^90, then a NaN | still a lower bound in Python integers; NaN rejected |
| control: port written at the end of B, undone in the first early tail | passes the B+tail screen; harness `compensation-changed`; `audit_local` endpoint failure |
| #1018's seven slots on the pre-slot word `db2c7cfb` | −1788 surrogate units each, −12516 together; certified true gains of −1784.83 each, −12493.80 together |
| source-holder fusion + full read-set exchange at slot sites X=439, X=444 | −3957 each |
| five slots + both fusions | −16854; `audit_local` PASS; unchanged interfaces; κ 0.001672756914849856 on #1094's owners |

`exchange.py` also regenerates the published SW4 word from the promoted word, as a self-check of the exchange family.

## Usage

The README covers the modules, a workflow (price → search → compose/transplant → admit), and the model and pitfalls, e.g.:
- the unpin step that `freeze_spec.py` needs after a word change;
- `emit_allcold.py` reading `SPEC.data.plan_sha256` directly;
- `evidence/local` in the gauge44 T16 packages being historical #645 files.

On the pre-slot k8 word, `repair.py --workers 6` sweeps 2,405 fusions in about 6 minutes; the only negative surrogate
deltas are the two sites above. With `--interval` (about 8 minutes), no other priced candidate can gain more than 3.3e-11
units at b. `REVISION2-REGRESSION.json` compares both revisions on this sweep.

## Scope

Search output is nomination data. A construction exists only after the unchanged package chain admits it, as in #1195.

The certificates are per-instance statements at the stated endpoint b. Neither the global recursive moment root nor κ is
inferred from cost units: both are recomputed by `kappa.py` and the package chains.

The inherited all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, precision/tape,
analytic-transfer and bit H1–H5 assumptions remain. This is not a formal proof of the multiplication theorem.

**Stacked on #540** (base branch `stack/pr540-base` = #540 head `acc19170`). Once #540 lands, this PR retargets to `main`. It adds one directory, `research/lean-pending-derivation/`. **No #540 file is changed**, so #540's hashed manifests and receipts stay valid.

## What it closes
#540's `PhysicalSourceConnection.pendingTag` supplies the pending ranges `[15,22)` and `[1,29)` by hand. Its README notes that "neither Lean nor the source-extraction check binds these ranges to the source schedule". #1228 derived them in Python. This PR does the derivation in Lean 4.21 and proves it equal to #540's actual definition.

## Theorems
All are proved by `decide`, using only `propext` and `Quot.sound` (some use no axioms).
- `PendingDerivation.idle_ranks_and_nesting`: for all 10 idle events, levels nest and the derived pending size equals the scheduled rank.
- `pending_child1 / pending_child2`: `[15..21]` and `[1..28]`.
- `hosted_windows`: for all 16 tags, stage 2 is in the child's window, the host pair is not pair 0, and `offset+width ≤ |pending|`.
- `target_derived`: every extracted `targetMask` is exactly the `[offset, offset+width)` slice of the derived pending axes. This also checks the extractor's hard-coded bases.
- `PendingBinding.pendingTag_derived` and `pending_eq_derived`: #540's `pendingTag` and `pending` equal the derived masks.
- `PendingBinding.selected_invocation_completion_derived`: #540's completion theorem, restated with the derived mask.

Definitions: L₋₁ = {0}, L_ℓ = [0,8) ∪ E₁ ∪ … ∪ E_ℓ (E_s = exterior axes of the stage-s route), pending = L_target \ L_source, and windows follow PR442's last-touch rule. The schedule and blocks are a Python-extracted literal (`generate_pending_schedule.py --check`, byte-exact against #540's pinned inputs). This is the same trust boundary as #540's other literals.

Six mutation controls each fail because `decide` refutes the mutated statement:
- L₋₁ empty;
- L₋₁ set to the whole local block;
- exterior blocks off by one stage;
- the first two blocks swapped;
- child 1 advanced before the selected call;
- child 1 claimed on the previous block.

## Not covered
- The level model is a definition. Its agreement with the PR386 frames (L₋₁ = span(q) in the `B_port ⊕ I₅₆` chart) is not proved. It is constrained only by ranks, nesting and the extracted target masks.
- Ascending axis order within a child is the offset convention shared with #540's extractor.
- Only one invocation is covered. No cost, all-size or κ claim.

## Reproduce
```sh
cd research/lean-multi-host-source && lake exe cache get <the five Mathlib modules in BUILD.md>
lake build PhysicalSourceConnection     # 3m24s measured on Apple silicon with the Mathlib cache
cd ../.. && python3 research/lean-pending-derivation/verify.py   # ~17 s, prints PASS_PR540_PENDING_RANGES_DERIVED_IN_LEAN
```
`verify.py` runs the generator check, compiles the three modules against #540's build through `lake env`, audits the axioms of all seven theorems and runs the controls.

**Credit:** the Lean formalization, ownership literals and gap identification are cheesegrader's #540. Construction and hosting are from #434/#442, and the bit geometry is from PR386. The Python predecessor is #1228. Prepared by Douglas Colkitt with substantial Claude (Anthropic) assistance. Apache-2.0.

> **What is claimed, and what is not.**
> **Scope.** The k8 / #1018-type local word of the E8 complex unit: 112 targets with ports u_t ∈ F₂⁹ (distinct, odd weight, u·u = 1), frames that are subspaces of F₂⁹, the verifier rules R1 (an ADD climbs both operands to one frame), R3 (frames are monotone) and E (every target register ends in perp(u_t)); fixed ports, fixed decoder, fixed targets (`gk_word.py:116`, `:102`, `:117`; `audit_local.py:137-138`, `:122`, `:115`, `:142`). The deletion experiments run on the gauge-forward word of that skeleton (the stage before the port, cold44 and layer stages), regenerated by `verify.sh` from vendored inputs; the census, bound and window rows run on the #1018 word.
> **Result.** (T, argued from the cited rule lines; instances checked) A direct read `y_t += s` at time τ forces the end frame of y_t to contain D_s(τ), the join of every frame register s had before τ; y_t must end in perp(u_t), so the read is legal only if D_s(τ) ⊆ perp(u_t), and otherwise one of four prices is paid: (a) a version of s (held or reconstructed), (b) a reorder that puts the offending operations after τ, (c) a FULL end or descent on the target (a rank unit per call), (d) a descent on s. (M) Deleting any of the 24 legal single S3 packet copies, the 16 hub copies or any of five larger families (up to 80 copies) leaves 4 to 64 targets ending FULL, one dimension outside perp(u_t), and no complement sink can host a FULL frame; all 30 distinct regenerated words pass the generator's own frame check and fail the verifier's end rule E (`gk_word.profile` run on two of them, the end-cap replay on all). (P) One unit costs −2.819% κ per call (linear to 32 units; no exact certificate at 35) against a helper worth ≈ +0.15% and a ceiling of +3.5152% for all 112 S4 copies, so a copy is about 19 times cheaper and the copies are economically forced where the obstruction fires. (E) The escapes we built are closed in their stated models: one-accumulator version reconstruction (0 orders, exhaustive over the 20-21 op cluster, four absorption variants), the snapshot hoist and slide (0 of 64, 0 of 86), rematerialising the 161 never-read helpers (0 of 65), coded target pairs and cold-slot holds (0 of 224), and the frame-conflict bound (111 helpers forced, 113 attained; #1140 proves a stronger 224 on the same word).
> **Not claimed.** No κ gain, no word, and no proof that the 268 S3/S4 copies are necessary for every skeleton or op multiset. The theorem is a necessary-condition and pricing statement for the verifier model above. It does not exclude **two accumulators** (+1 helper per group; not searched), a **new h = 8 family** (needs a different decoder; C.6 gives none at window ≤ 9 for the current one), **joint deletion and reordering** at scale (only single hoists and slides were run), asymmetric pairings that unpin Lemma R, non-projection rational labels, or helpers (arbitrary ends via `helper_final`). No deletion word passes the chain, so no κ is computed for one.

Knowledge package `research/end-cap-obstruction/`, in the layout of #899: one `verify.sh`, a hard-failing step 0 (every file against `MANIFEST.sha256`, every vendored input against `SOURCES.json`: git blob ids, and for the #1018 word the hash that #1018 publishes), vendored pinned inputs, and every CHECKED row re-run from them.

```sh
python3 -m pip install -r research/end-cap-obstruction/requirements.txt
bash research/end-cap-obstruction/verify.sh /fresh/output/dir     # from a checkout or `git archive` of the whole repository
```

## Results (26 rows: 19 CHECKED, 4 ARGUED, 3 RECORDED)

| id | result | status |
|---|---|---|
| T1-T3 | Read-drag lemma, the end-cap theorem with its four prices (a)-(d) and the last-hop argument, the version corollary (a snapshot is not enough when s is written between the drag and τ). The rule lines they use are read from the vendored files at the cited lines (19 anchors). | ARGUED; anchors CHECKED |

1. **Two accumulators:** terms join only inside their pair, y170 reads both; +1 helper per group (owner re-plan), estimated to eat most of the credit; rescue check is a second accumulator in `cards/B256/dfs.py` (not run).

Fresh `git archive` of the commit, every assertion PASS, exit 0: **91 PASS lines (2 in step 0), 0 FAIL, about 8 minutes wall** on 12 cores of a shared machine (the four exhaustive orderings searches of group G5 set the wall time; everything else is under 90 s).

## Change and mathematical scope

PR1048 compares profiles at a fixed exponent without establishing the ordering of their actual roots. This package reproduces the maintainers' counterexample, supplies a certified surcharge-inclusive reference-root comparator, and independently excludes improvement by at most two transports in the explicitly frozen PR589 domain.

The complete census contains **1,452,893 legal single transports** and **59,998 distinct overlapping ordered operation pairs**, giving **1,379,084 final pair representatives**. Singles have 1,227,676 exact ties and 225,217 strictly worse outcomes; pair representatives have 1,282,055 exact ties and 97,029 strictly worse outcomes. Both implementations report **zero better and zero unresolved cases**. Repeated-operation and register-disjoint pairs are covered by the accompanying reduction proof; operation-pair counts are not literal path counts.

The comparator encloses signed `J_delta` over the entire verified reference-root bracket using outward rational transcendental bounds. It fails closed on uncertain signs. This is a finite audit, with no new construction or κ improvement. Three or more moves, growing catalogues, arbitrary subspaces, other circuit identities, illegal intermediates, and full multiplication-theorem/native/precision obligations remain outside scope.

Start with [the result and exact domain](research/pr1048-complete-feasibility/README.md) and [the proof](research/pr1048-complete-feasibility/PROOF.md).

## Task and overlap

Explicit Brian Ross assignment: repair PR1048 pricing and independently check post-first-move coverage. Scope was refined from a bounded diagnostic slice to complete exclusion in the declared frozen domain: 3,064 elementary A/B operations; frames from the original 636-frame catalogue plus each current slot's own rational lower-span closure; legal intermediates and resulting retained COPY constraints.

Base: `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`. Retained dependencies: #1048 at `07730cd8302c378607259a9ad0efb73e0b57a2f2` and #1182 at `0213b8911bfeefd5c81ddf320bac6a0fb7e86215`, with unchanged sources and notices. Four additive research directories; no existing upstream source or selected construction changes. Earlier package narratives and receipts are preserved as historical evidence.

Ian Libânio's #933 at `b9348c6907516e55dc07e135ad4d7a480d4f9840` already reports broader relocation/all-frame negative results and a 2,000-pair independent sample. This contribution claims no first-negative priority or equivalence with that larger domain. Its added value is corrected reference-root pricing, the explicit pair-projection completeness argument, and a full separate replay of this narrower domain. See [publication checks and overlap](research/pr1048-complete-feasibility/PUBLICATION.md).

## Validation

CPython 3.13.2 on macOS. Reproduction commands and pinned receipts are in the README and [independent review](research/pr1048-complete-feasibility/REVIEW.md).

- All 36 mandatory input pins pass. Separate implementations agree on every single-operation domain, the full pair transcript, all 93 pair delta/count/status records, and enclosing price intervals.
- Complete primary/independent pair scans took 372.174/125.896 seconds. A fresh isolated independent full replay on the submission base took 119.384 seconds and matched the saved complete result.
- Transcript SHA256: `b39d6d23210ab7eee24c04e165b078e39ea00053e4be4b523f7c793e24b79679`.
- Existing root-ordering and bracket defects reproduce. Semantic corruption controls fail closed. A synthetic strict-improvement control demonstrates why equal first-state profiles cannot justify discarding continuation neighborhoods; it is not an improving PR589 witness.
- `python3 -I -B scripts/verify_selected_result.py` and diff whitespace checks pass.

No full selected cold replay, native admission, repository-wide historical suites, hosted CI, proof assistant, or independent human proof review is claimed.

## Credit

Prepared by Brian Ross with OpenAI Codex assistance, including separate GPT-6 Astra review and rerun. Credit flemhhh's original search; Douglas Colkitt/the maintainers' existing counterexample; woklerx's reused #1182 bracket repair; Ian Libânio's #933; and DreamingOfClouds, eumemic, and retained supplier lineage.

Brian Ross's [Krenn independent verifier](https://github.com/brianross93/Krenn/blob/ab446724a61a293a3268c63b9e9e721c6a360561/experiments/krenn_quantum_graph/independent_verifier.py) and [semantic-corruption tests](https://github.com/brianross93/Krenn/blob/ab446724a61a293a3268c63b9e9e721c6a360561/tests/test_krenn_artifacts.py), plus [ThetaTwist exact-arithmetic discipline](https://github.com/brianross93/thetatwist/blob/b4ec6c13088b89961834cc675b44b81372199b02/src/thetatwist/core.py), inform the methodology. This is methodological adaptation, with no copied code from those projects or PR933. Existing licenses are retained; new material is Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

The [smallest useful follow-up](research/pr1048-complete-feasibility/README.md#open-next-questions) is a correspondence audit of PR933's first-slot equivalence and post-first neighborhoods against the pair-specific projection here. Different move primitives and global frame reoptimization prevent assuming equivalence. No defect in PR933 is asserted; no larger search is justified without a new completeness argument.
